papers.title: Exact mean first-passage time and a Poisson-smoothing crossover in renewal shot noise
papers.abstract: Threshold crossings in exponentially relaxing shot noise depend on the interplay between incoming impulses and the residual signal left by earlier arrivals. For renewal input, existing high-threshold product approximations of the mean first-passage time (MFPT) leave open when evaluation at a single index preserves the mean with vanishing relative error. Here we derive an exact finite-threshold MFPT series for exponentially marked renewal shot noise and recast it as an average over an auxiliary Poisson index. When the waiting-time density exhibits short-time power-law behavior, $w(t)\sim ct^{\kappa-1}$, the dominant series contributions shift from the Poisson center by an amount of order $x^{1-\kappa}$, whereas the averaging kernel has a fluctuation width of order $\sqrt{x}$, with $x=\lambda b$. The competition between these scales yields a crossover at $\kappa=1/2$, where the deterministic-index product is asymptotically exact in ratio above this boundary, requires a finite multiplicative correction at criticality, and exhibits a growing logarithmic discrepancy below it. A moving-saddle approximation also yields an asymptotically exact MFPT ratio under general strictly positive, finite-mean waiting times. Numerical comparisons across Gamma, Weibull, and generalized-Gamma renewal laws illustrate the approximation regimes and their finite-threshold accuracy. Together, these results provide an exact finite-threshold benchmark for the mean first-passage time and reveal how short-gap renewal statistics determine the asymptotic accuracy of high-threshold approximations.

papers.title: Application-Oriented Evaluation of CPU/GPU Quantum Simulators: From Foundational Circuits to Quantum Chemistry
papers.abstract: Quantum computing simulators underpin the development and prototyping of quantum algorithms, yet the practical choice between competing software stacks and their CPU and GPU backends is rarely guided by application-oriented evidence. We present a systematic, quantum hardware-agnostic evaluation of two widely used stacks, CUDA-Q and Qiskit, selected as the simulators closest to production execution paths, across CPU and GPU backends, and across single- and double-precision arithmetic. The evaluation spans foundational utility circuits (GHZ-state preparation and QFT/QFT$^\dagger$ mirror circuits) through applied quantum chemistry (Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) energy estimation with standard UCCSD and a depth-reduced LCNot-UCCSD ansatz, and direct sampling on hydrogen chains up to 32 qubits). The results yield concrete selection guidance: GPU-accelerated double precision delivers consistent speedups, typically $2\times$ to $10\times$ for tractable application workloads and substantially larger at the widest circuits up to $100\times$ or more, and governs the maximum simulable system size under fixed compute memory, while CPU statevector backends and Qiskit Aer remain competitive, and at times preferable, at low qubit counts and wide but shallow circuits. We demonstrate the practical payoff of this guidance by extending an in-house developed QSCI(LCNot-UCCSD)-RBM electronic-structure workflow, previously constrained to a 16-qubit active space on a CPU, to a 32-qubit (10 electrons, 16 orbitals) active space with GPU acceleration, completing a 20-point potential-energy-surface scan of N$_{2}$ in the cc-pVDZ basis. This end-to-end evaluation establishes that the principled simulator selection translates directly into expanded scientific reach and faster algorithmic prototyping.
authors: Anurag K. S. V., Ashish Kumar Patra, Afra Navas, Ruchika Bhat, Sai Shankar P., Rahul Maitra, Manas Mukherjee, Jaiganesh G

papers.title: Kalb-Ramond black bounces: throat-blind shadows and throat-sensitive neutrinos
papers.abstract: Regularizing a black hole removes its singularity, but which observations could detect the regularized core? We address this question for a Simpson-Visser black bounce built on the power-law hairy black hole that a Lorentz-violating Kalb-Ramond background produces. Measured in the areal radius, the bounce leaves the metric function untouched and changes only the radial measure. This single fact sorts the observables into two classes. The shadow, the innermost stable orbit, orbital frequencies and gravitational redshifts are blind to the throat. The instability of the photon ring, the brightness of its subrings, the oscillation phase of neutrinos and the energy deposited by neutrino pair annihilation respond to it through one universal factor. We derive an exact law for the subring demagnification that holds for any metric function. We also show that the throat enters the weak-field neutrino phase and the light deflection with different weights, so that combined photon and neutrino lensing can separate the mass from the throat. Ray-traced polarized images of a turbulent thin disk confirm that the direct image hides the throat while the first subring reveals it. For neutrinos emitted near a stellar-mass compact object the throat reshapes the flavor survival pattern and enhances the annihilation energy deposition. Two independent computations reproduce each headline number.

papers.title: Metric perturbations in Einstein-Hilbert gravity: An alternative perturbative formulation
papers.abstract: We derive the ordinary gauge-fixed quadratic operators of the four-dimensional Einstein--Hilbert action in exponential and inverse-metric-density variables on an arbitrary reference background. With a single nonlinear background-harmonic gauge transported through the exact field map, the density operator is the trace-reversed Lichnerowicz operator, while the exponential operator contains an additional algebraic Ricci-curvature term. This difference arises from the nonlinear transformation of the background tadpole and vanishes on Ricci-flat backgrounds; a cosmological-constant check gives the corresponding cancellation at Einstein saddles. The construction retains the exact determinant contribution and specifies the associated Faddeev--Popov operator. At the first interacting order on a flat background, we show that the two gauge-fixed cubic actions differ by a term proportional to the free field equation, and independently evaluate the same nonzero three-point coefficient in both variables, with its normalization matched to the Einstein-gravity interaction. An exact Schwarzschild configuration satisfies the same background-harmonic gauge and is stationary under unrestricted exterior variations of the gauge-fixed action. Its density and exponential reconstructions are checked together with the bulk and boundary terms; a separate radial variation illustrates the loss of an equation after imposing a restricted ansatz. These results provide an explicit comparison of established field coordinates at the classical and tree levels; quantum loop calculations additionally require a common measure, regulator and source prescription.

papers.title: Thermodynamics and interior structure of density-responsive regular black holes
papers.abstract: This work studies regular black holes motivated by the scalar sector of density-responsive gravity (DRG). An algebraic prescription with phenomenological local running maps a Gaussian matter profile to a diagnostic density profile. A pressure check shows that this profile does not solve the full static DRG equations. It serves only to select an effective metric family with two horizons. The extremal mass is calibrated to $M_{\min} = \sqrt{1+A/2}\,M_{\mathrm{P}} \simeq 1.006\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$, where $A=0.024$ is the historical scalar response amplitude. A fit to $\rho(r) = \rho_0\exp[-(r/r_c)^n]$ selects $n=2$. The temperature is nonmonotonic, reaching $T_H^{\max}=0.02547\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$ at $M=1.332\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$ before vanishing at $M_{\min}$. The calculation verifies the generic scaling near extremality $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{tr}}\propto(M-M_{\min})^{-1/2}$ of a static lapse diagnostic for $n=2,3,4,6$ and for the Hayward and Bardeen controls. A regulated integral of coordinate time between the horizons provides a static cavity diagnostic, not a prediction of echoes of gravitational waves. The remaining area entropy equals the area entropy already lost at $M_{\mathrm{cross}}/M_0=0.707107\simeq1/\sqrt{2}$. This geometric crossing does not establish a Page curve or unitarity. The endpoint area entropy is below $2.6\%$ of the initial Bekenstein-Hawking entropy for $M_0 = 5\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$ and below $0.03\%$ for $M_0 = 50\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$. An inverse source reconstruction confirms an isotropic core of de Sitter type but retains the pressure mismatch. An exploratory collapse calculation with an imposed bounce factor produces bounded configurations with $1-2m/r<0$ without establishing formation of the calibrated geometry. The robust results are the calibrated thermodynamics and generic scaling near extremality.

papers.title: Holographic Einstein rings of a covariant quantum corrected AdS black hole
papers.abstract: We investigate holographic Einstein rings in a covariant quantum corrected Schwarzschild--AdS$_4$ spacetime using a massless scalar probe. At fixed horizon radius $r_h$, the deformation parameter $\zeta$ leaves the metric mass parameter, coordinate surface gravity, and photon sphere radius unchanged, while increasing the photon potential maximum and the asymptotic lapse coefficient $A=1+\zeta^2$. The critical coordinate impact parameter approaches $A^{-1/2}$ for large black holes, whereas the corresponding incidence angle in the normalized boundary frame approaches $\pi/2$. Ray tracing and local WKB barrier data recover the same geometric scale. Quasinormal spectra computed with AdS boundary conditions provide a comparison at finite multipole number. These results separate the finite radius effect of the deformation from the change in boundary time normalization.
authors: Zhenglong Ban, Xiaomei Liu, Rong-Jia Yang

papers.title: Liquid-liquid criticality in a fluid whose two structures favor mixing
papers.abstract: The generic two-state description of liquid polyamorphism requires a non-ideality opposing mixing for liquid-liquid separation. This condition assumes that the free energy of the underlying fluid is independent of the structural order, an assumption that fails when the local structures differ in size or attraction. We derive a closed-form stability condition after density relaxation for a van der Waals closure based on the second virial coefficient of a pair potential whose internal state determines both the contact distance and the well depth. The condition recovers the familiar result for structures identical in size and attraction but can change sign within the liquid when they differ. In ten of the thirty-four parameter sets examined, a critical state preferred by the liquid requires a non-ideality favoring mixing. For one such fluid, we construct the coexistence curve, which terminates at the predicted critical point at positive pressure. Attraction and excluded volume provide distinct contributions to the density-order coupling; only the former survives on a fixed lattice with single occupancy. Removing the excluded-volume contribution restores the familiar condition in 58 of the 82 such critical states found. Thus, within this closure, liquid-liquid separation can occur with a non-ideality favoring mixing.

papers.title: Directional gate-error asymmetry and universal selectivity bounds in non-unital open quantum systems
papers.abstract: Clifford randomized benchmarking and average gate fidelity assign a single trajectory-independent decay rate to a noisy quantum gate at leading order in the dimensionless damping exposure \varepsilon = \gamma T, concealing state-dependent transition-error asymmetries in untwirled quantum circuits. While state-dependent amplitude-damping errors are well known in open quantum systems, a trajectory-level analytical framework that bounds directional transition selectivity across arbitrary pulse shapes and Markovian environments has been lacking. Using first-order toggling-frame perturbation theory for a two-level qubit coupled to a Markovian bath, we show that the antipodal survival-error slopes \chi_+ and \chi_- along any piecewise-continuous control path depend exclusively on its time-averaged Bloch vector m and transverse residence covariance matrix G, obeying the complete-positivity cofactor bound \beta(r) \le 1. On a standard polar \sqrt{X} gate, longitudinal T_1 relaxation induces a 12.23 : 1 directional survival-error split (\kappa_{T_1} = (3\pi - 8)/(3\pi + 8) \approx 0.081767), whereas time-symmetric X rotations maintain an exact 1 : 1 balance (\kappa_{T_1} = 1). Across all completely positive Markovian generators, coupling between non-unital drift and unital diffusion enforces a selectivity bound \kappa_\star = (\pi - 2\sqrt{2})/(\pi + 2\sqrt{2}) \approx 0.052456 (19.06 : 1) for time-independent single-qubit \pi swaps. We apply this framework to Gaussian and derivative-removal-by-adiabatic-gate (DRAG) waveforms on superconducting transmons and trapped-ion qubits, extend the analysis to finite damping, pulse dwell, colored thermal baths, and qutrit leakage, and construct two-branch differential lock-in protocols that isolate directional error splits immune to first-order state-preparation and measurement errors.

papers.title: A Beginner's Guide to Physical Networks
papers.abstract: Network theory studies entities (nodes) and the relationships between them (edges). While these entities and their relationships may be abstract in general, this tutorial focuses on the special case of physical networks: spatially embedded networks that carry physical quantities such as electric charge, fluid volume, or momentum. The underlying structure is described mathematically by a graph (Section I), with the incidence matrix playing a central role in the analysis. Viewing a graph as a special case of a cell complex reveals the topological structure of the incidence matrix and its relation to familiar operators from calculus (Section II). Because these networks are physical, flows are conserved at each node and often derive from the gradient of a potential. Models that satisfy these principles behave analogously to circuits; accordingly, we first review circuit theory (Section III), then examine related fluid flow (Section IV) and mechanical (Section V) networks. Briefly, the topics of random walkers (Section VI) and nonlinear networks (Section VII) will be discussed, followed by concluding remarks (Section VIII). Analytical examples and Python implementations, in lieu of pseudocode, are included throughout. Exercises are included as footnotes. This tutorial is based on a short course taught at the Boulder School for Condensed Matter in 2019 and a course taught at the University of Pennsylvania in Spring 2024. It should be a useful resource for students, teachers, and researchers applying graph theory to physical networks. Knowledge of linear algebra is assumed, but no prior knowledge of graph theory or physics is necessary.

papers.title: Quantum-inspired orthogonal adapters for certifiably robust medical image classification
papers.abstract: Medical image classifiers require not only high accuracy but also reliable predictions under small input perturbations. Certified robustness provides mathematical guarantees of prediction stability, but preserving these guarantees when adapting pretrained models to new tasks remains challenging. We propose a fine-tuning approach based on quantum-inspired orthogonal butterfly layers that preserves the Lipschitz bounds of pretrained certified networks. Inspired by quantum circuits of reconfigurable beam splitters, these layers preserve orthogonality by construction using only $\mathcal{O}(n\log n)$ trainable parameters. Their structured design enables efficient classical implementation and offers a path toward future quantum implementations with logarithmic circuit depth under suitable connectivity assumptions. Controlled experiments on MNIST and MedMNIST demonstrate improved certified robustness compared with conventional alternatives and, in the DermaMNIST transfer, greater resistance to the tested attacks than low-rank adaptation (LoRA). We then apply it to trichoscopic image classification for alopecia diagnosis and alopecia areata activity assessment. By adapting a certified ImageNet-pretrained network, butterfly fine-tuning achieves approximately twice the certified accuracy of conventional fine-tuning and LoRA, with comparable classification accuracy on the same backbone and data split and similar empirical resistance to the tested adversarial attacks. Larger robustness guarantees, including certificates covering certain image-processing transformations, can be obtained at the cost of reduced accuracy. These results highlight the potential of quantum-inspired butterfly layers for parameter-efficient adaptation of medical image classifiers while preserving the mathematical guarantees underlying certified robustness.
authors: Olga Tsurkan, Laia Domingo, Victoria Orlova, Asel Sagingalieva, Iris Zalaudek, Raffaele Dante Caposiena Caro

papers.title: Quantum Transitions From Integrable to Chaotic
papers.abstract: The quantum integrable-to-chaotic transition is commonly pictured as the quantum counterpart of the classical Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser (KAM) scenario: a phaseout transition in which a family of regular eigenstates coexists with, and gradually yields to, chaotic eigenstates. Here we show that this is not the only fundamental route from integrability to chaos in quantum systems. We identify a second elementary transition---the morphing transition---which has no classical counterpart: all eigenstates hybridize and turn chaotic concurrently, so that no regular subsequence survives at any stage of the crossover. The two transitions are spectrally distinct: the phaseout spectrum is an independent superposition of regular and chaotic subsequences with Berry-Robnik statistics and a finite short-spacing intercept $P(0)$, whereas the morphing spectrum exhibits global level repulsion with Lenz-Haake statistics and $P(0)=0$. We demonstrate both transitions, and their mixture, in three models. The results for the deformed boson model further show that the quantum phaseout scenario is conditional on a smooth quantum-classical correspondence.

papers.title: Relativistic and quantum fluid dynamics: nonlinear momentum evolution
papers.abstract: We present an alternative framework for nonlinear momentum evolution in fluid dynamics, in which relativistic effects are proposed as an underlying mechanism for nonlinear behavior, even in the low-velocity regime. By interpreting the second-order velocity diffusion equation from a quantum-mechanical perspective, we establish a connection between higher-order viscous transport and the reduced Planck constant, identifying the second-order viscosity coefficient with \(\hbar\). Furthermore, we show that the coupling of second-order velocity diffusion and nonlinear momentum evolution leads to a Dirac-type equation for quantum fluids. These findings reveal a potential connection among relativistic effects, higher-order fluid transport, and quantum wave dynamics.

papers.title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
papers.abstract: We present a nonperturbative lattice study of vacuum decay through bubble nucleation in a three-dimensional real scalar field theory at finite temperature. The vacuum decay rate is computed by combining an expanded-ensemble multicanonical hybrid Monte Carlo approach, which samples the critical bubble configurations, with real-time Langevin dynamics, which follows the subsequent bubble evolution. We extrapolate the nucleation rate to the continuum limit and compare it with the corresponding one-loop perturbative prediction, finding a discrepancy of about \(8\%\).

papers.title: Observables and Symmetries in Causal Fermion System
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay of observables and symmetries in the framework of causal fermion systems (CFS). We show that position observables transform covariantly under unitary symmetries and for static CFS we derive their Heisenberg-type evolution. To give these results a geometric interpretation, we establish conditions under which spacetime isometries induce symmetries of CFS constructed from solutions of the Dirac equation. The crucial link is provided by the Dirac equation itself, which relates the infinitesimal generators of the geometric and CFS symmetries. In static spacetimes, this allows us to identify the generator of the induced unitary symmetry with the spatial Dirac Hamiltonian.
authors: Patrick Fischer, Claudio F. Paganini, Sahil Yadav

papers.title: A treatment of d-dimensional Coulomb-Sturmians with noninteger quantum numbers and their connection to the radial momentum operator
papers.abstract: The Bagci-Hoggan exponential-type orbitals, the generalization of Coulomb-Sturmians to noninteger quantum numbers, were recently identified as d-dimensional Coulomb-Sturmians. In the present study, this identification is treated in detail. The radial differential equation for these orbitals is derived directly from their closed form. It represents the general Coulomb-Sturmian differential equation for quantum numbers with real values. The solution is verified through a power series representation and a first-order matrix form based on the Green's function of the radial Laplacian. New transformation relationships between these orbitals and Slater-type orbitals with noninteger principal quantum numbers are established. The radial differential equation is expressed in terms of the radial momentum operator. The expectation values of the position and radial momentum operators are obtained in closed form. The radial and Heisenberg uncertainty products, the Shannon entropy and the Fisher information are derived in general form.

papers.title: Schwarzschild scattering from CFT
papers.abstract: We show that retarded CFT correlators on $\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{S}^2$ in a state described by the small black hole in AdS$_4$ can be used to derive asymptotically flat Schwarzschild partial-wave S-matrix elements, including its spectrum of quasinormal modes. This is achieved by identifying a class of operators for which the dual bulk fields behave as plane waves near the AdS boundary for sufficiently high frequencies. For such operators there is a simple analytic relation between CFT correlators and reflection coefficients which behaves gracefully in the flat space limit, $L\to \infty$. These include spin-1, spin-2, and conformally coupled scalars. We provide a simple toy model that captures how dissipative QNMs can appear for short times inside Hermitian systems, closely resembling the small black hole in AdS.

papers.title: Gravitational Memory Correlators and BMS Symmetry
papers.abstract: We compute the n-point memory and mixed energy-memory correlators for scalar decay into gravitons using the in-in formalism at leading order in perturbative quantum gravity. We obtain compact results for arbitrary n and explicitly verify the supertranslation flux balance relation between memory, energy, and Bondi mass detectors, realizing asymptotic symmetry constraints on infrared-finite observables.
authors: Enrico Herrmann, Ian Moult, Brett Oertel, Julio Parra-Martinez, Biswajit Sahoo

papers.title: Optimal Frobenius light cones for power-law systems in any dimension
papers.abstract: We prove optimal Frobenius Lieb-Robinson bounds for power-law systems with power-law exponent $\alpha$ in any dimension $d$, in particular showing that the algebraic to linear light cone transition occurs at $\alpha=d+1$. The proof uses a spectral clipping method and concentration result to allow for running a multiscale operator-norm argument which produces the optimal Frobenius norm exponent. Additionally, we prove there is a Frobenius light cone transition from polylogarithmic to algebraic at the summability threshold $\alpha=d$, and a transition from decaying in volume to non-decaying in volume at $\alpha=d/2$.
authors: Laura Shou, An Le, Twesh Upadhyaya, T. C. Mooney, Alexey V. Gorshkov

papers.title: Determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $\beta$ decays using effective field theory
papers.abstract: A precision determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $\beta$ decays requires exquisite control over radiative corrections, including nuclear-structure-dependent effects whose evaluation has traditionally relied on nuclear models. To assess the uncertainties inherent in the nuclear matrix elements, an alternative strategy based on effective field theory (EFT) has been established in recent years. Here, we present material progress in this program, in terms of a first EFT calculation of the crucial correction $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$ for 12 superallowed transitions ranging from $^{10}$C $\rightarrow$ $^{10}$B to $^{54}$Co $\rightarrow$ $^{54}$Fe. These main results rely on nuclear ab initio calculations using the coupled cluster method, benchmarked against Quantum Monte Carlo evaluations for light nuclei. The global fit to superallowed decay rates reveals that the precision in $V_{ud}$ is currently limited by short-distance contributions that in the EFT are parameterized as two-nucleon contact interactions, leading to an uncertainty $\delta V_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$. We discuss the consequences for the status of the first-row unitarity test of the CKM matrix as well as a roadmap how to reduce the uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ in the future.
authors: Samuel Novario, Graham Chambers-Wall, Vincenzo Cirigliano, Wouter Dekens, Jordy de Vries, Stefano Gandolfi, Martin Hoferichter, Emanuele Mereghetti

papers.title: Rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising models from a tetrality web
papers.abstract: We construct rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising (TIM) models by using different chiral symmetries to prepare their folded boundary states. We use a moving up procedure which extends the product theory to an auxiliary coset with an $S_3$ automorphism group, where permutations give twisted Cardy states. We complement this with a moving down approach which reduces to the $S_3$ invariant algebra. Overall, these procedures uncover a tetrality web relating four different theories. Pulling back ordinary Cardy states of the smallest theory in the web to the physical tensor product system gives eighteen factorized interfaces and six transmitting interfaces. The latter agree with four transposition and two 3-cycle twisted boundaries in the largest theory. They include Gaiotto's RG wall and the interface obtained by fusing an Ising duality line into it. The six interfaces carry the regular action of the TIM fusion ring and have the same energy transmission coefficient, $35/48$. Their boundary entropies, bulk correlations and operator spectra distinguish them. We calculate these observables and the complete annulus amplitudes between the twenty four boundaries.
authors: Ant\'onio Antunes, Jin Chen, Junchen Rong

papers.title: Constants and Nonperturbative Corrections in $V^{5,2}$ Theories
papers.abstract: We study perturbative and exponentially small corrections to the on-shell effective twisted superpotentials of two three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ theories associated with free and fixed-locus cyclic quotients of the non-toric Sasaki-Einstein manifold $V^{5,2}$. These are the two-node Chern-Simons theory at levels $(k,-k)$ and the one-node flavored theory with $N_f$ fundamental pairs, respectively. At superconformal chemical potentials, we propose the Chern-Simons counterpart of the all-order perturbative expression for the flavored theory and obtain convergent integral representations for the rank-independent constants of both theories. At integer parameters, these constants admit explicit evaluations involving finite sums of Clausen functions and $\zeta(3)$, while their large-parameter expansions Borel sum to the defining integrals. At $k=1,3$ and $N_f=1,3$, we conjecture complete exponential remainders expressed through Eichler integrals of weight-four Eisenstein series. Supported by high-precision Bethe solutions, the resulting completions coincide at unit quotient order but differ at order three. We determine the minimal modular levels of the Eisenstein generators and establish convergence and natural boundaries for their primitives. Within the relative M-theory localization prescription, a complementary bulk analysis recovers the Chern-Simons shifted rank and constant in the $b\to0^+$ limit of the squashed-sphere partition function. We propose a generalization incorporating fixed-locus contributions that yields the corresponding flavored-theory result. The two theories therefore share a modular structure in their nonperturbative coefficient laws, but distinct perturbative shifts and exponential corrections resolve differences invisible in their common leading $N^{3/2}$ behavior.

papers.title: Quantum Cooling by Classical Shadows
papers.abstract: Cooling to ground states of many-body Hamiltonians by imaginary-time evolution is central to quantum simulation, but its non-unitary aspect prevents direct implementation on a quantum computer. Existing routes restore it by importing structure from outside the intrinsic quantum dynamics, e.g. by parameter estimation on many copies or recursive compilation. Here, we show that a single randomized snapshot of the quantum many-body system is sufficient to steer the state along the cooling direction on average. Our algorithm, shadow chain, uses randomized measurements to collapse the state to its classical record, which fixes the next unitary update. Snapshots across steps form a trajectory that is a quantum-executable sample of an auxiliary-field path integral; fluctuations among trajectories are exponentially suppressed in system size. With the randomness supplied intrinsically by the Born measurement rule, the trajectories sample themselves rather than going through external accept-reject steps. The resulting algorithm is ansatz-free and exact upon extrapolation to the continuous limit, with the exponential cost confined only to system size rather than temperature.

papers.title: Quadratic Sum Rules for Scalar Amplitudes
papers.abstract: Kleiss--Kuijf and Bern--Carrasco--Johansson relations, and their string monodromy generalizations, have long provided some of the most powerful and useful constraints on partial amplitudes. Motivated by their success, we uncover a new class of quadratic-sum rules that connect scalar amplitudes at different multiplicities. Combining recursion, kinematic shifts, and symbolic regression, we establish them for the nonlinear sigma model and its string-inspired extensions. We then extend these relations to diagonal elements of the inverse Kawai--Lewellen--Tye matrix and subsequently to planar scalar theories with nonderivative interactions and general propagators.
authors: Karol Kampf, Ji\v{r}\'i Novotn\'y, David Podiv\'in, Jonah Stalknecht

papers.title: Generalised global symmetries of 6d SCFTs on a circle from the blow-up equations
papers.abstract: We study 6d $(1,0)$ SCFTs on a circle, possibly twisted, through the blow-up equations of their 5d descriptions. For every theory we consider, we construct the explicit map between the 6d and 5d frames, including the ratio $r$ of the Kaluza--Klein (KK) mass to the instanton mass, which depends on the frame and not only on the twist. Our main result is that the higher-form symmetries of these theories, their mixed anomalies and 2-groups can all be read off from the fluxes through the exceptional curve of the blown-up $\mathbb{C}^2$. The flux sectors are the 't$~$Hooft sectors of the 5d 1-form symmetries. On the tensor fluxes, the 6d Green--Schwarz couplings fix the weights, whose fractional exponents we read as the mixed anomalies of the 6d 2-form symmetry with the KK $\mathrm{U}(1)$, gravity, flavour and $\mathrm{SU}(2)_R$. The fluxes forced in each sector decide between a 2-group and a mixed anomaly. For instance, the twisted frames $\mathfrak{su}(4)_{0,4}+4\Lambda^2$ carry a non-split $\mathbb{Z}_4$ 2-group, while, in $\mathfrak{su}(4)_2+4\Lambda^2$ and $\mathfrak{su}(4)_6+2\Lambda^2$, the instanton symmetry is locked to the flavour centre and only a mixed anomaly remains. The same method applies to the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ gauging of two, three and four copies of the $E_1$ theory, which describes, respectively, $\mathrm{SU}(4)_0$, pure $\mathrm{Spin}(8)$ and the untwisted $\mathfrak{so}(8)$ KK theory. There, the fluxes exhibit the extensions of 1-form symmetries inherited from the $E_1$ 2-groups, identify the states that break each accidental 1-form symmetry and the background to which it is locked, and give the 5d 2-group to which the $S_3$-invariant 6d 3-group reduces.

papers.title: Metamorphic Testing of Quantum Software based on Stabilizer States
papers.abstract: A major challenge in quantum computing is to systematically check if a quantum program implements its desired functionality. For classical programs, testing is widely used; each test case comprises a pair of sample input and expected output to be compared with the actual output. To increase the number of test cases, however, one has to solve the test-oracle problem: for each additional test input one has to know the correct output. Metamorphic testing tackles this problem by utilizing metamorphic relations between input and output domains to automatically derive new test cases from existing ones. However, adapting metamorphic testing to the quantum realm is not straightforward, since quantum states cannot be directly inspected. We propose a framework of quantum metamorphic testing (QMT) in which the metamorphic relations incorporate the measurement procedures required to assess quantum outputs. We apply our QMT framework to testing the preparation of stabilizer states, which are central to protocols like measurement-based quantum computing or quantum error correction. We utilize structural properties of stabilizer states to systematically derive measurement circuits for new test cases from existing ones. We implement this framework in Qiskit, and demonstrate that it reduces by an order of magnitude the testing run time compared to testing with randomly generated input states. We further show effectiveness by revealing synthetic program faults injected by circuit mutations, as well as a real bug in the Qiskit compiler.
authors: Adri\'an Mar\'in Boyero, Fynn Otto, Albert Rico, Otfried G\"uhne, Malte Lochau

papers.title: Universal Quantum Computation in a Wigner's Friend Framework
papers.abstract: The Wigner's Friend thought experiment illustrates a core tension in quantum mechanics: an observer inside an isolated laboratory (the Friend) measures a definite outcome, while an external observer (Wigner) describes the laboratory as a coherent superposition. Here we show that this discrepancy, usually studied as a conflict between descriptions, has a direct computational consequence. We namely propose a protocol by which Wigner can turn the Friend's laboratory into a universal quantum computer, whereby the Friend is restricted to apply simple classical operations within the laboratory. We also experimentally implement a proof-of-principle demonstration of this protocol for single-qubit gates using single photons. By recasting the coherence between incompatible descriptions as a computational resource, we thus link the foundations of quantum measurement to quantum computation.
authors: Mart\'i Cladera-Rossell\'o, Sebastian Horvat, Borivoje Daki\'c, Lee A. Rozema, Philip Walther

papers.title: Gapless Nature of Spin Liquid in the $S=1/2$ Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet with Neural-Network Quantum States
papers.abstract: Whether the spin-$1/2$ kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet hosts a gapped $\mathbb{Z}_2$ or a gapless $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquid remains a central open question in frustrated magnetism. Here, we address this question by directly computing the triplet gap with a neural-network quantum state that does not presuppose any specific spin-liquid structure. Applying a time-reversal symmetric transformer-based ansatz to clusters of up to $768$ sites, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies on two-dimensional lattices with periodic boundary conditions and estimate an energy per site of $-0.43873(12)$ in the thermodynamic limit. Finite-size scaling of the magnetic order parameter and triplet excitation gap shows that both extrapolate to zero in the thermodynamic limit. Together, these results provide independent and direct evidence of a gapless spin-liquid ground state, consistent with the $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquid. More broadly, they demonstrate that neural-network quantum states can resolve ground-state properties of frustrated quantum magnets that remain challenging for conventional numerical methods.
authors: Andreas Raikos, Alessandro Sinibaldi, Riccardo Rende, Giuseppe Carleo, Federico Becca, Luciano Loris Viteritti

papers.title: Non-Topological Chiral Anomaly: The Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect
papers.abstract: We derive the chiral anomaly in a thermal medium and show that, in addition to the well-established topological piece, the anomaly acquires a previously overlooked non-topological contribution, relevant for non-gauged axial symmetries. Remarkably, this modification of the continuity equation is independent of the electromagnetic fields, thereby giving rise to novel transport effects in relativistic hydrodynamics. We further propose an experimentally accessible new effect in Weyl semimetals which we call the Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect: an electric field proportional to the magnetic field is generated by the non-topological anomaly, even in the absence of an externally applied electric field. Beyond this concrete prediction, our results establish a broader hydrodynamic framework for non-topological chiral anomalies, opening the door to a range of previously unexplored anomaly-induced transport phenomena across condensed-matter and high-energy systems.
authors: R\'emy Larue, Amaury Marchon, J\'er\'emie Quevillon, Diego Saviot

papers.title: Skyrmions coupled to the sigma meson
papers.abstract: We propose a geometric coupling of the Skyrme model of nuclei to the scalar--isoscalar sigma meson by identifying the sigma field with the radial length of the chiral four-vector while preserving the topological protection of the baryon number. Restricting to the $B=1$ hedgehog ansatz, an asymptotic analysis of the field equations shows that the in-vacuum sigma mass $m_\sigma$ is replaced inside the nucleon by an effective in-medium mass $m_{\sigma,{\rm eff}} = 2m_\pi$. Full numerical integration via a double-shooting method and parameter optimization demonstrate that including the sigma meson leads to a remarkable improvement in the description of nucleon observables and to a pion decay constant very close to its physical value.
authors: Christoph Adam, Carlos Naya, Thomas Winyard

papers.title: Ab initio calculations of ${\bar\delta_\text{NS}}$ and extraction of ${V_{ud}}$ using effective field theory
papers.abstract: Radiative corrections limit the precision of $V_{ud}$ extractions from superallowed $\beta$ decays. In particular, the model dependence in the nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) is difficult to assess without a clear organizing principle, which is provided by effective field theory (EFT). We report substantial progress in this program based on ab initio nuclear calculations using the coupled cluster method. Benchmarking results against Quantum Monte Carlo calculations for light nuclei, we evaluate all two-body NMEs that enter the correction $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$ across 12 superallowed transitions relevant for $V_{ud}$, including an estimate of truncation and Hamiltonian uncertainties. We find that certain three-body NMEs at ${\mathcal O}(\alpha^2)$ play an important role, due to a combination of large numerical prefactors and coherent scaling with $Z^2$. We develop a formalism to estimate such NMEs based on nuclear densities to complete the EFT evaluation of $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$, validating the corresponding two-body NMEs against ab initio calculations. We further identify the corrections in the traditional phase-space factor that are captured by the EFT and remove them consistently, which renders the individual transitions mutually consistent. Profiting from a recent calculation of ${\mathcal O}(\alpha^2 Z)$ ultrasoft photons, we find that the scale uncertainty in the EFT is now negligible, while the remaining uncertainty is dominated by contact terms required to renormalize the magnetic Gamow-Teller NMEs. One combination of low-energy constants can be determined from a global fit to the superallowed data, but the second one proves strongly correlated with $V_{ud}$, necessitating additional input to resolve the nuclear-structure effects. We argue that such short-distance contributions currently imply an uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ at the level of $\delta V_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$.
authors: Samuel Novario, Graham Chambers-Wall, Vincenzo Cirigliano, Wouter Dekens, Jordy de Vries, Stefano Gandolfi, Martin Hoferichter, Emanuele Mereghetti

papers.title: Flexible ground-state search algorithm on hybrid Clifford-tensor network manifolds
papers.abstract: Tensor network algorithms face challenges in highly entangled regimes, such as systems with periodic boundary conditions (PBC), long-range interactions, or higher dimensions, where the required bond dimension quickly renders computations infeasible. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a novel approach that integrates the stabilizer formalism directly into the traditional density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) algorithm. While previous methods have used Clifford unitaries to minimize ground-state entanglement, fundamentally limited to distilling that away utilizing local two-qubit operations, our framework optimizes Clifford transformations to minimize the state's energy. We benchmark our method against standard DMRG at fixed bond dimensions for the Ising model on a ring (including long-range interactions) and on a torus. We observe systematic gains in models with local interactions - as drastic as a factor of 40 decrease in bond dimension in two dimensions. Our algorithm is readily implementable in standard DMRG codes and provides a practical way to substantially reduce algorithm costs, paving the way for large-scale simulation at volumes beyond what is presently achievable.
authors: Hari Timsina, Antonio Francesco Mello, Meghadeepa Adhikary, Marcello Dalmonte, Mario Collura

papers.title: Modified scattering and asymptotic completeness for a massive Dirac-wave system in dimension three
papers.abstract: We establish global well-posedness and modified scattering for the three-dimensional Dirac-Klein-Gordon system with a massive spinor and a massless scalar field, for small, sufficiently regular and localized initial data. This answers a question posed by Dong, Li, and Yuan in \cite[Case IV]{DLY23}. We also identify a Majorana-type condition on the initial data that yields linear scattering, showing that both linear and modified scattering solutions coexist in this model. Conversely, we establish asymptotic completeness for small asymptotic profiles satisfying suitable regularity and decay assumptions. The forward argument combines the hyperboloidal foliation method with testing by wave packets, whereas the backward construction relies on a contraction argument in suitably chosen norms.

papers.title: A Quasipolynomial Quantum Algorithm for the Vector Dihedral Coset Problem with Smooth Modulus
papers.abstract: We give a quantum algorithm for the vector dihedral coset problem over $\mathbb{Z}_q^n$, in which the goal is to recover $\mathbf{s} \in \mathbb{Z}_q^n$ given independent samples of the form $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bigl(|{0,\mathbf{x}}\rangle+|{1,\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{s}}\rangle\bigr)$, for $\mathbf{x}\sim \mathbb{Z}_q^n$. When the modulus $q$ is $B$-smooth, the algorithm uses $n^{O(B^{1+o(1)}\log q)}B^{O(B^{2+o(1)}\log q)}$ samples and time. For $B = \mathrm{polylog}(n)$ and $q=\mathrm{poly}(n)$, this gives a quasipolynomial time- and sample-complexity. This extends the previously known quasipolynomial-time result for power-of-two moduli (Bonnetain, Naya-Plasencia, ASIACRYPT 2018; Bai, Jangir, Kirshanova, Ngo, Youmans, CRYPTO 2025). The algorithm proceeds by reducing the modulus one prime factor $p | q$ at a time. The key ingredient is a sieving procedure that clears the non-linear terms in the phase modulo $p$ via an algorithm of Ivanyos, Santha (TCS 2017) that finds non-zero $\mathbf{u} \in \mathbb{F}_p^\ell$ such that $\sum_{i \in [\ell]} u_i^d \mathbf{a}_i = 0 \mod p$ for degrees $1 \le d \le p-1$, given vectors $\mathbf{a}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{a}_\ell \in \mathbb{F}_p^n$ as input. The algorithm also applies to the extrapolated dihedral coset problem (EDCP) introduced by Brakerski, Kirshanova, Stehl\'e, Wen (PKC 2018), which is known to be equivalent to LWE in the polynomial sample regime. However, our result does not yield a new attack on LWE in any regime, precisely because the known reduction from LWE to EDCP provides only polynomially many clean samples, whereas our algorithm requires quasipolynomially many samples. The main algorithm was obtained in a GPT-5.6 Sol conversation prompted by the author; the author is responsible for all statements, proofs, and correctness. Concurrent work of Boucher, Fouque, Shen gives an algorithm with similar guarantees for prime-power moduli.

papers.title: Beyond the Onsager matrix: All-order resummation of relativistic particle and energy diffusion
papers.abstract: We study the coupled diffusion of particle number and energy carried by ultrarelativistic probe particles propagating through a material medium. The probes undergo elastic scattering, which randomizes their direction, and inelastic scattering, which exchanges energy with the medium while preserving particle number. We compute exactly the full $2\times2$ frequency- and wave-number-dependent diffusivity matrix, resumming the constitutive gradient expansion to all orders. In a particularly natural Onsager-normalized basis of conserved densities, the resummed matrix is found to be diagonal at arbitrary frequency and wave number, even though particle and energy transport remain coupled and the conventional Onsager matrix has nonzero thermoelectric cross coefficients. Beyond the hydrodynamic limit, the resummed diffusivities resolve microscopic relaxation timescales and the ballistic kinetic continuum that are invisible to the ordinary Onsager coefficients.

papers.title: Coupling-Response Thermodynamic Density of States for Bosonic Working Media
papers.abstract: We introduce an operational thermodynamic density of states (TDOS), $\mathcal{G}_\lambda=(\partial S/\partial\lambda)_{T,\mu}$, to characterize bosonic working media under microscopic spectral control. At fixed chemical potential, the response is strictly driven by the structural density of states, yielding the exact scaling law $\mathcal{G}_\lambda=-(d/\alpha)S/\lambda$ for homogeneous spectra $\epsilon(k)=\Delta+\lambda k^\alpha$, while coupling-dependent gaps generate edge terms only for finite boundary weight. Under a fixed-particle constraint, a secondary chemical-potential redistribution channel emerges. Exact solutions for quadratic bands and harmonic traps demonstrate that spatial dimensionality dictates whether this constrained TDOS exhibits a jump discontinuity or remains continuous across the Bose--Einstein condensation threshold. For pure scale control, the response maps exactly to the heat capacity, $\lambda \mathcal{G}_\lambda^{(N)}=-C_N$. This framework is applied to evaluate reversible work in Stirling cycles and to identify observables in magnonic platforms, contrasting global spectral edges with topological Dirac gaps in honeycomb ferromagnets.
authors: Francisco J. Pe\~na, Bastian Castorene, Nicolas Vidal-Silva

papers.title: Landauer erasure and horizon information in an expanding universe
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic cost of information erasure in Friedmann--Robertson--Walker cosmology by combining Landauer's principle with the thermodynamics of the apparent horizon. Adopting the apparent-horizon temperature as an effective cosmological temperature, we find that for standard non-phantom expansion, the minimum heat required to erase one bit decreases while the entropy-equivalent information content of the horizon increases. We further compare the Landauer heat with the Misner--Sharp energy and show that, despite their simple thermodynamic relation, they have distinct physical meanings. These results provide a simple connection between information erasure, horizon thermodynamics, and gravitational energy in an expanding universe.

papers.title: Double-Randomized Quantum Singular Value Transformations For Early Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers
papers.abstract: The Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT) is an algorithmic framework which encompasses a wide range of problems, including Hamiltonian dynamics, ground state preparation, Gibbs state preparation, amplitude amplification, and matrix inversion. For many areas of scientific interest such as quantum chemistry and condensed matter, the circuit depth of the block-encoding subroutine in QSVT can be formidable, limiting the scope of problems to which QSVT can be applied on early fault-tolerant hardware. We split linear operators $A$ into a core operator $A_0$ and a tail operator $A_\epsilon$, block-encoding the normalized sum of $A_0$ and the average of $n_T$ randomly sampled terms from $A_\epsilon$. We show that using randomized block-encodings of this form allows one to lower the circuit depth of QSVT while incurring a diamond norm error that scales as $\mathcal{O}(C_P\delta^2/n_T$), where $C_P$ is a prefactor which depends on the QSVT polynomial $P$ and $\delta$ is the ratio of the $\ell_1$ norms of the coefficient vectors of $A_\epsilon$ and $A$. We then go on to show that if one samples QSVT circuits from a joint probability distribution of both random block-encodings and random polynomials (Double-Randomized QSVT), then the circuit depth savings of these two randomization techniques combine multiplicatively, with only additive error contributions. We numerically calculate error bounds for long-range Heisenberg and iron-sulfur complex Hamiltonians, showing that for a diamond norm error bound of $10^{-3}$, RBE-QSVT can reduce the number of Pauli terms needed for the block-encoding by an order of magnitude or more in several cases. This paves the way for demonstrations of QSVT on early fault-tolerant hardware.
authors: Joel Bierman, Pawan Poudel, Yuan Liu

papers.title: Gate tunable spin splitting for Andreev spin qubits in Ge quantum well heterostructures
papers.abstract: Ge-based super-semi heterostructures are a promising platform for implementing Andreev spin qubits (ASQs). For example, they can be isotopically purified to eliminate nuclear spins that cause decoherence. However, spin-orbit coupling (SOC), which is a key ingredient for ASQs, is cubic in momentum for hole-based materials like Ge, in contrast with more-conventional ASQ materials (e.g., InAs wires), for which the SOC is linear in momentum. In this work, we study the interplay between geometrical properties like the channel width, and gate-tunable properties like the chemical potential, on ASQ operations. Intriguingly, we find that the spin splitting in a planar Ge Josephson junction does not depend on the junction width, in contrast with InAs nanowires. We explore the possibility of exploiting this property to suppress the harmful effects of charge traps. However, this prospect is spoiled by the fact that charge traps also affect the chemical potential, in addition to the channel width. Our results provide insights into the fundamental mechanisms governing spin splitting in ASQs and offer guidance for optimizing ASQs in other materials with cubic SOC.
authors: Avani Vivrekar, Benjamin D. Woods, Mark Friesen

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of axisymmetric perturbations of near-horizon extremal Kerr with a Schwarzian-deformed throat
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic stability of axisymmetric gravitational perturbations of the near-horizon geometries of (near-)extremal Kerr black holes and consider the family of backgrounds in which the AdS$_{2}$ factor of NHEK is deformed by a Schwarzian mode. Requiring the Killing parameter to be local in the background makes the Gelfand--Dikii polynomials natural solutions of the Killing equation, and that locality requirement brings stationary solutions of the Korteweg-de Vries equation. The hierarchy selects a family of backgrounds, which remain $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})\times \mathfrak{u}(1)$ throughout them: the first level gives NHEK and near-NHEK, the second, solitons that depart from one of these geometries and return to it. We linearize Einstein's equations around this family, where the axisymmetric sector reduces to a wave equation on the nearly-AdS$_{2}$ base, and analyze this equation by energy and virial methods. For NHEK we obtain a conserved energy, an integrated local energy estimate and asymptotic stability in a weighted norm; for a nonconstant Schwarzian the energy becomes a Lyapunov functional whose monotonicity is dictated by the sign of its derivative, yielding uniform bounds for integrable ones, and mild local decay along the KdV soliton. We also find a monotone horizon-localized norm, which is not of Aretakis type, showing that stability properties are directly sensitive to the near-horizon structure encoded in the Schwarzian background. We compute the associated Regge--Teitelboim charges at a late-time corner of the throat using a radial ADM foliation of the spacetime.
authors: Marcela C\'ardenas, Benjam\'in Cuevas-Tapia, Claudio Mu\~noz, Jessica Trespalacios, Hanne Van Den Bosch

papers.title: Certifying quantum generative models beyond the Fisher trace
papers.abstract: Whether a trained quantum generative model has learned its target is usually decided by a diagnostic validated on a labeled benchmark, and such a diagnostic can pass that validation by recovering how the benchmark was built. We analyze Fisher-trace and kernel-based certification of the real-amplitude quantum circuit Born machine in noiseless statevector simulation. For real-amplitude circuits built from half-angle rotations, the classical Fisher information equals the quantum Fisher information almost everywhere, so its trace equals the parameter count and carries no information about fit quality. The Fisher eigenvalue rank counts the live nodes of the amplitude tree: it coincides with the label on a sparse benchmark and is uninformative on a full-support one. The pooled Wasserstein and maximum-mean-discrepancy scores move with optimizer convergence and with the scoring convention. For two bitstring defect families on which both metrics have closed forms, we compute the tolerance-mismatch window in which the discrepancy rejects generators that the transport threshold admits; it opens only at certification-grade tolerances and closes as the qubit number grows. On the Hamming cost we prove a sharp tolerance ratio above which the discrepancy vote is redundant, and we obtain the exact worst-parity minimax value over all unit-diagonal positive-semidefinite kernels, which is exponentially small in the qubit number. In a numerical campaign at the tolerances a near-term experiment can resolve, the discrepancy vote changed no verdict at a thousand shots or more. The false-pass guarantee does not extend to device noise.

papers.title: Accelerating Atomistic-Continuum Simulations of Multilayer 2D Materials with Functional Principal Component Analysis-Based Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Atomistic-continuum simulations of complex wrinkling deformations in large-area multilayer two-dimensional (2D) materials are computationally expensive. To accelerate these simulations, this work presents a machine-learning (ML) framework that first constructs a low-dimensional representation of the deformation field, then learns the deformation in this reduced space. Dimensionality reduction of deformed 2D membranes is challenging because of the extremely high dimensionality of discretized deformation fields, the need to preserve surface continuity and prescribed geometric constraints, the stochastic nature of wrinkling patterns, and the limited availability of training data. We address these challenges using two-dimensional functional principal component analysis (FPCA). The proposed FPCA representation reduces deformation fields containing millions of degrees of freedom to latent spaces with only tens of dimensions while preserving the continuity of the deformed surface. In addition, prescribed homogeneous boundary constraints are satisfied exactly through an appropriate choice of basis functions in the FPCA representation. A neural network is then trained to predict the principal components from the system and loading parameters. The resulting ML-predicted deformation fields are used as high-quality initial configurations for the atomistic-continuum solver, which subsequently performs energy minimization to obtain equilibrium solutions. The framework is demonstrated for multilayer graphene subjected to uniaxial compression, biaxial compression, and combined biaxial compression and simple shear. For the most computationally intensive large-strain cases, the proposed approach achieves speedups of at least 6.8 times while converging to final energies comparable to, and in some cases lower than, those obtained using conventional atomistic-continuum initialization.
authors: Jonathan Oleson, Abhishek Keripale, Shashank Pathrudkar, Susanta Ghosh

papers.title: Hidden Momenta due to Magneto-Electric Coupling in Non-Reciprocal Media
papers.abstract: From a canonical quantisation approach of macroscopic quantum electrodynamics, we derive the interaction Hamiltonian due to a dipole emitter interacting with a time-symmetry-broken topological insulator (TSB-TI), described by an axionic coupling Lagrangian. This provides an additional interaction term dependent on the magneto-electric coupling strength inherent to the TSB-TI which will modify measurements on related observables. The spontaneous decay rate is calculated in the Born-Markov approximation for a general electromagnetic Green's tensor, and then specifically for the case of a planar parallel-plate cavity.
authors: William S. McGregor, Niclas Westerberg, Robert Bennett

papers.title: Gravitational and Maxwell--Proca-Type Structures in a Variational Metric-Affine Framework
papers.abstract: We study Einstein's nonsymmetric metric-affine Lagrangian density with a generally nonsymmetric metric and an affine connection treated as independent variational variables. The resulting connection equation belongs to the classical Einstein--Hlavat\'y--Tonnelat framework, while the unrestricted metric Euler--Lagrange equation is analyzed without a divergence constraint on the antisymmetric metric density. Its symmetric part takes the form of Einstein-type gravitational equations with geometrically induced source terms and reduces to the vacuum Einstein equations in the torsion-free limit. The antisymmetric part becomes a geometric constitutive relation based on the irreducible decomposition of torsion. Its contracted four-divergence yields a general vector-field equation with geometric source and response terms. Under a trace--axial reduction, $Q=0$ gives a source-free Maxwell-type equation, whereas constant nonzero $Q$ gives a Proca-type equation. Independently, a trace of the generalized Bianchi identities yields the homogeneous Maxwell-type pair associated with the torsion trace, while the connection equation implies a Lorenz-type condition. Thus gravitational, constitutive, Maxwell--Proca-type, and Lorenz-type structures arise as compatible consequences of one metric-affine variational system. The antisymmetric dynamical level is generated by the contracted four-divergence of its constitutive level. No independent electromagnetic or matter field is introduced.

papers.title: Quantum Coloring Games on Complete Graphs
papers.abstract: We study the nonlocal game where two players are both given an input ($x$ and $y$, respectively), from a set of size $n$ and, without communicating, must give outputs $a$ and $b$, respectively, from a set of size $m < n$, winning when $(x = y) \leftrightarrow (a = b)$. This can be considered a graph coloring game on the complete graph with $n$ vertices. In the simplest case, the players get random equal inputs with probability $\frac{1}{2}$ and random unequal inputs otherwise. We solve this case of the game, and many others, for both classical and quantum (i.e., where the players may share finite-dimensional entangled quantum states) strategy sets, proving the value (the probability of winning) of the optimal strategies and providing explicit strategies that attain this optimum for all $n$ and $m$. Our optimal strategies are synchronous: i.e., the two players always give equal outputs when given equal inputs. These strategies remain optimal when the probability of receiving equal inputs is at least $\frac{2}{m + 2}$. Across this wide range of cases, we find that quantum strategies have an advantage over classical strategies exactly when $m$ does not divide $n$; this advantage is $O\left(\frac{m}{n^2}\right)$.

papers.title: Beyond global density in a stochastic sandpile: the role of spatial signatures in the predictability of extremes
papers.abstract: In self-organized critical systems the global load is a strong precursor of extreme events. In the two-dimensional Manna sandpile, grain density alone predicts extreme avalanches with an AUC of about 0.96. We ask whether density fully determines the system's readiness for an extreme event, that is, whether microstates with the same number of grains are equivalent. Because density is such a strong predictor, a method that sees the full microstate can score well just by counting grains. We therefore compare only states with an identical number of grains. Even then, both a parameter-free statistic and a convolutional network distinguish states that precede an extreme avalanche from typical ones, while shuffled controls do not. The signal is a load contrast between the center and the dissipative boundaries, carried by the two lowest symmetric cosine modes. Their normalized energy is a single variable that needs no training. Together with density it recovers most of the gain that a network trained on the full microstate achieves over density alone. Readiness for an extreme avalanche therefore depends both on the total load and on how that load is distributed relative to the boundaries.
authors: Kamil P. Orzechowski, Julian Sienkiewicz, Piotr Fronczak

papers.title: Witnessing Magic (and other Quantum Resources)
papers.abstract: Motivated by measurements of quantum magic, we study the sampling cost of resource robustness ---a quantifier for a broad class of quantum resources--- by bounding the variance of optimal robustness witnesses. We first lower bound the samples required to estimate a state's resource robustness using Cram\'er-Rao bounds. We find that the number of measurements scales at least quadratically in the robustness for highly mixed states, and at least linearly in the generalized robustness for broad families of pure states, making it difficult to measure either robustness to low absolute error when the states are highly resourceful. We then derive two complementary bounds in terms of the geometry of witnesses, one of which is tight for a class of resource theories including coherence and bipartite entanglement. An additional hurdle occurs for tracking the onset of resource robustness along state-space trajectories: the integrated witness variance along a path is at least the squared resource gain over Fisher length, indicating that a state evolution with exponential resource gain necessarily goes through states for which the robustness cannot be measured efficiently. This hurdle does not occur when estimating robustness to fixed relative, rather than absolute, error. These results suggest that the ideal witness-based resource estimation task, for general resource theories, is the estimation of generalized robustness to low relative error on highly resourceful pure states.

papers.title: Finite-time quenches across first-, second-, and infinite-order transitions in XXZ spin chains
papers.abstract: We investigate how equilibrium quantum phase transitions manifest themselves in small systems driven out of equilibrium by quantum quenches. We consider linear ramps of the anisotropy in spin-1/2 and spin-1 XXZ chains, which host transitions of first, second, and infinite (Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless, BKT) order. We consider system sizes available in current quantum simulators and investigate how the order of the transition, the symmetries, and the ramp duration affect the decomposition of the time-evolved state into the instantaneous eigenbasis. The order of the transition determines the dynamics: across the BKT transition, moderately slow ramps already keep the system close to its ground state, corresponding to an adiabatic evolution, whereas for the second-order Haldane-N\'eel transition a ramp roughly three times slower is required to reach the same regime. Across the first-order transition, since the dynamics conserves the magnetization of the initial state, we observe the formation of ferromagnetic domains, separated by a single domain wall for slow ramps and by multiple walls for faster ones. Interestingly, shortly after the transition, the state evolves as a coherent beating between domain-wall states, a behavior captured by the recently proposed quantum-state texture.
authors: Luiz Felipe Santos Dittberner, Luigi Berber, Maria C. O. Aguiar, Krissia Zawadzki, Helena Bragan\c{c}a

papers.title: Control of Non-Markovianity via Channel Exceptional Points in a Driven-Dissipative Kerr-Cat Qubit
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) in open quantum systems are conventionally defined at the Liouvillian level, making them representation-dependent and often requiring auxiliary degrees of freedom. We study EPs directly at the quantum-channel level in a driven-dissipative Kerr-cat qubit, in which dissipation drives bidirectional jumps between its two basis states. Interpolating two Markovian channels yields single EPs when the endpoints straddle a spectral-phase boundary and, remarkably, double EPs within the same phase. The interpolated EPs map out a Markovian--non-Markovian phase diagram: the parameter plane separates certified non-Markovian and Markovian domains, with domain boundaries switching the channel between the two characters. Three spectral criteria certify every domain. As the evolution time advances, the domains drift, split, and partially shrink, making the switching increasingly sensitive to parameters and time. This establishes a representation-independent paradigm for classifying and switching quantum memory effects, applicable to continuous-variable, discrete-variable, and hybrid systems.
authors: Tian-Le Yang, Hao-Long Zhang, Pei-Rong Han, Zhen-Biao Yang, Shi-Biao Zheng

papers.title: A Bound on Wormhole Probing Time from Holographic Multi-Entropy
papers.abstract: Bipartite entanglement entropy eventually saturates and therefore cannot track the continued growth of an eternal wormhole. Recently, it was shown that genuine tripartite multi-entropy can probe wormhole growth even after bipartite entanglement entropies have saturated. This naturally raises the question: can increasing the number of parties extend the probing time indefinitely? Adopting the multiway maximin prescription and assuming that its selected representatives are regular spacetime-stationary networks, we prove that the answer is no for nonrotating BTZ black holes. We establish a common finite upper bound on the probing time for every fixed finite boundary partition, independent of the number, sizes, and arrangement of its parties. For any network on any Cauchy slice, there exists a comparison network that assigns the entire central region containing the wormhole interior to a single party. A network longer than this comparison network cannot minimize length on that slice. The central length required by a stationary network connecting the two boundaries grows with time, whereas the central length of the comparison network remains uniformly bounded. At sufficiently late times, such a network therefore cannot minimize length on any Cauchy slice containing it and is excluded from the maximin prescription. Consequently, beyond this bound, no network selected by maximin enters the black-hole interior.

papers.title: Spacer-Engineered Spectral Selectivity in Metal-Carbon Solar-Thermal Absorbers
papers.abstract: Spectrally selective solar-thermal absorbers must capture sunlight while limiting emission at operating temperatures where the Planck spectrum overlaps the solar band. We connect this trade-off to a controlled optical mechanism in a metal-carbon metasurface. A radiative-limit calculation using AM1.5D illumination identifies how cutoff wavelength, infrared absorptivity and concentration together constrain equilibrium temperature, while the metasurface calculations reveal the additional role of a sharp spectral transition. We then separate the dielectric gap from the absorbing carbon layer in a gold--carbon architecture. Frequency-domain fields and material-resolved dissipation show that the spacer controls the overlap of a gap-localised mode with carbon, extending the high-absorptivity band and sharpening its infrared roll-off. A thickness sweep demonstrates that the spectrum with the strongest visible absorption need not give the highest radiative-limit equilibrium temperature. Polar-angle- and polarisation-resolved calculations demonstrate the angular robustness of the proposed plasmonic metasurface and assess the extent to which normal-incidence spectra approximate hemispherical emission. The calculated high-temperature values are benchmarks for the fixed-geometry, fixed-optical-constant model, not operating temperature predictions for the gold structure. The study establishes spacer-controlled loss partitioning as a route to shaping solar-thermal spectra and distinguishes optical selectivity from materials durability and useful heat output.
authors: X. Romain, A. P. Vafa, M. Florescu

papers.title: Machine-learned active spaces enable quantum calculations of spin-state energetics of transition-metal complexes on quantum hardware
papers.abstract: Multireference calculations on transition-metal complexes, on classical or quantum hardware, depend on the choice of active space. The orbitals that belong in it are those that are strongly entangled in the correlated wavefunction, but measuring this entanglement requires the very correlated calculation that the active space is meant to make affordable. Here we present SpinAware, a machine-learning model that predicts density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) single-orbital entropies and orbital-pair mutual information from the unrestricted Hartree-Fock (UHF) solution of each spin state, without any correlated calculation. Each of the 20 highest occupied and 20 lowest unoccupied orbitals is described by 60 descriptors computed from the UHF solution, among them the differences between its alpha and beta occupations and energies, its metal-d and ligand character, and its exchange coupling to the other orbitals, and a transformer predicts the entropy of each orbital in the context of all others. Trained on 3454 spin-pure DMRG calculations on mononuclear Cr-Ni complexes, the model transfers to experimentally characterized complexes with ligands, binding topologies, oxidation states and metals absent from training. Over 11 spin states it reproduces the DMRG entropy profiles with a mean absolute error of 0.027, and combining the predicted entropies with the predicted mutual information gives a candidate pool that contains 99% of the DMRG-active orbitals of the benchmark spin states while keeping, on average, only 15 of the 40 orbitals. Natural-orbital occupation scans then select compact active spaces from this pool for a nickel and a cobalt complex. Sample-based quantum diagonalization with samples from IBM quantum processors reproduces the exact CASCI energies of these spaces to within 0.3 kcal/mol and their spin-state gaps to within 0.10 kcal/mol for up to 32 qubits.
authors: Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Thomas D. K\"uhne, Sabre Kais, Werner Dobrautz

papers.title: Slow and rapid mixing in $\mathbb{Z}_2$ hyperlattice gauge theory
papers.abstract: The Ising model under Glauber dynamics on the torus is known to exhibit a phase transition in its mixing time. The mixing is exponentially slow when $\beta >\beta_c$ and logarithmically fast when $\beta <\beta_c$. In this paper, we generalize the slow-mixing result to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ hyperlattice gauge theory when $\beta$ is large enough. This is a higher-dimensional analogue of the Ising model, with spins on $k$-cells. Specifically, on the torus of any dimension $m \ge k+2$, we prove explicit exponential lower bounds on the mixing time of Glauber dynamics when $\beta$ is sufficiently large. More precisely, we prove that the result holds for a broader class of dynamics, allowing more than one $k$-cell to change its value at each step of the algorithm. Finally, we show that there are distinct slow and rapid mixing regimes, as for sufficiently small $\beta$ the Dobrushin condition is satisfied for Glauber dynamics under the heat-bath rule, which implies logarithmic mixing.

papers.title: Quasi-particle sector hybridization and the onset of chaos in spin ladders
papers.abstract: How quasiparticle numbers influence the emergence of quantum chaos is a fundamental question in interacting many-body systems. We investigate this interplay in a spin-$1/2$ XXZ ladder, where the strong-rung regime supports an approximate organization of many-body eigenstates into quasi-particle(triplon) number sectors. Using spectral statistics, triplon-based observables, and von Neumann entanglement entropy, we characterize the microscopic hybridization of triplon-number sectors as the leg coupling increases. We find that the crossover toward Gaussian orthogonal ensemble statistics shifts to weaker couplings with increasing system size, whereas the characteristic crossover scale associated with triplon-sector hybridization exhibits a much weaker size dependence. Furthermore, eigenstate-to-eigenstate fluctuations exhibit scaling consistent with the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis even while remnants of the strong-rung structure persist, suggesting that spectral chaos does not necessarily require complete sector hybridization.

papers.title: Projected DKP spin-1 sectors in a $(2+1)$-dimensional static wormhole: Self-duality, helicity content, and spectral correspondence
papers.abstract: We use the projected spin-1 Duffin--Kemmer--Petiau (DKP) equation in $2+1$ dimensions to clarify the physical content of the irreducible $3\times3$ representations. The projected antisymmetric tensor is algebraically dual to the projected vector, and the two twin representations select conjugate self-dual covariant-curl sectors, which reduce to opposite massive helicities in the flat-space limit. We then apply this structure to the static wormhole problem previously studied with a single irreducible representation. The first-order radial DKP system contains an exceptional normalizable bound-state branch at $\omega^2=M^2$ that is absent from the master-variable reduction, whereas the generic master and circular sectors are related by a Darboux transformation. The latter preserves the transmission and reflection probabilities, while the quasinormal modes are organized into two pole families in the complex radial-momentum plane, leading to the physical pairing $(\omega,-\omega^*)$ rather than a global $\pm\omega$ prescription.

papers.title: Stochastic gauge fixing from the holographic renormalization group
papers.abstract: We extend the dictionary between stochastic quantization and holographic Wilsonian renormalization to Yang-Mills theory in four-dimensional anti-de Sitter space at tree level. The radial component of the bulk gauge field is Zwanziger's gauge-fixing function; radial gauge is Parisi-Wu quantization, whose random walk of gauge modes is the longitudinal bulk propagator. We obtain the triple- and quadruple-trace couplings of gluons at finite cutoff in closed form. On transverse data, their dependence on the bulk gauge resides in a single zero mode, which drops out of the flat-space limit.

papers.title: The fate of hidden symmetries under magnetic Harrison transformations
papers.abstract: Solution-generating transformations construct new geometries from known seeds, raising the question of whether and to what extent the resulting solutions inherit the hidden symmetries underlying the seeds' integrability and separability. We have established universal perturbative inheritance laws for CKTs and massless scalar separability directly at the level of magnetic Harrison transformations, encompassing both magnetization of Carter-type seeds and demagnetization of conformal Carter-type seeds. In both magnetized Kerr and demagnetized Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson, this perturbative inheritance coexists with the loss of exact Carter-type separability, while seed-connected conformal Killing-Yano structures are already obstructed at the same perturbative order. These results reveal a hierarchy in the perturbative survival of hidden symmetries and provide a framework for investigating their inheritance in more general theoretical settings and under other solution-generating transformations.
authors: Shoulong Li, Fangkang Yu, Hong-Da Lyu

papers.title: Constrained Adiabatic Quantum Programming
papers.abstract: To find a $k$-clique in a graph, adiabatic quantum computation (AQC) evolves a quantum system from the minimum of an initial cost function to the minimum of a problem cost function that penalizes non-cliques. Existing AQC languages fix the initial cost function, so the search ranges over all $2^n$ subsets of the $n$ vertices, although only the subsets of size $k$ can be answers. We present ENQ+, an AQC language in which the programmer writes both cost functions. Data constraints define the problem cost function. Relational constraints, a new construct, declare the moves the search may make between configurations and define the initial cost function. For the clique, a single relational constraint, which exchanges a chosen vertex with an unchosen one, confines the search to the subsets of size $k$. ENQ+ thereby turns constrained quantum annealing, which physicists set up by hand for individual problems, into a programming construct. We give ENQ+ a semantics in many-world configuration (MWC) graphs, whose nodes are configurations and whose edges are moves, and derive from it a step-wise semantics of adiabatic evolution. We prove that a run stays within the component of the MWC graph that contains its initial state, and that a run from an approximate initial state still reaches the answer, with probability equal to its squared overlap with the exact one.
