These transformations are admissible for every Boolean network regardless of topology; for random-topology ensembles, including all ensembles of fixed in-degree $K<N$, they constitute the complete symmetry group. We also show that input-label permutations constitute a hidden gauge freedom of the dynamics. The Zyklenzeiger symmetry of Boolean functions follows directly from the node-flips of the hyperoctahedral group together with this gauge freedom. Boolean networks related by the hyperoctahedral group have isomorphic state-space networks and form its orbits, and Burnside's lemma gives the number of these orbits for any fixed network topology. It provides a symmetry reduction of the analysis of Boolean network dynamics and explains why the Boolean functions of evolved networks fall into Zyklenzeiger classes, and why these classes split in finite networks.

papers.title: A Numerical Approach to Quantization
papers.abstract: We introduce a numerical approach that simultaneously searches for matrix quantizations and compatible Poisson structures on classical geometric surfaces. Our method identifies irreducible Hermitian matrix representations and a trainable Poisson multiplier by minimizing a loss function that penalizes violations of the Casimir and commutation constraints. Through numerical investigations and subsequent theoretical analysis, we establish a no-go theorem showing that, for Weyl quantized fuzzy spheres with nondegenerate axial spectrum, the matrix dimension cannot exceed the degree of the nonconstant polynomial axial Poisson multiplier. We further extend our approach to nonpolynomial Poisson multipliers, demonstrating its versatility and potential to drive novel discoveries. Although here we focus on Weyl quantized fuzzy spheres, the framework is extensible to general geometric manifolds and quantization schemes. Our approach also provides a practical starting point for investigating Schild string theory and the quantization of spacetime histories.
authors: Grace Murray, Siyue Zhu, Angeline Hu, Kaitlyn S. Yasumura, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis, Trung V. Phan

papers.title: High-energy asymptotics for the spectral actions of free particles in thermal equilibrium
papers.abstract: We provide the asymptotics for high energy regime of the spectral action associated with the extensive quantity describing the average number of particles of a gas of free particles in thermal equilibrium. We analyse the case of massless particles (the massive non relativistic case being easier and well known) living in a finite volume manifold of arbitrary dimension, and subjected to periodic boundary conditions (i.e. the d-dimensional torus), obeying Bose, Fermi and Boltzmann statistics. We also treat in full generality the case of relativistic massive particles, which is more difficult and presents the appearance of a logarithmic term when the dimension of the underlying manifold is odd. The situation relative to massless and relativistic massive particles living on the 3-sphere is also studied, showing that, even in this case the asymptotics relative to the massive relativistic particles presents an analogous logarithmic term.

papers.title: Shallow Clifford circuits on square lattices
papers.abstract: We study the depth of CZ circuits, Clifford state preparation, and Clifford unitary synthesis over the two-dimensional square lattice. A programmable circuit on a $2{\times}k$ ladder ($n{=}2k$) implements an arbitrary CZ computation in depth at most $\frac{3n}{2}{+}3$ up to reversal of both rails. This improves the best-known LNN (Linear Nearest-Neighbor)-compliant depth-$(2n{+}2)$ construction by about 25\%. For state preparation, we consider a Phase gate programmable -H-{CNOT+P}-LC- circuit and derive matching obstructions to attaining the CZ-span counting lower bound of $2\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil{-}1$ for depth by the entangling gates. For cycle connectivity $C_n$, we prove that the minimum depth is exactly $2\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil{-}1$ when $n$ is not a multiple of four and $2\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil$ when $n\,{=}\,4k$. We construct a hole-free minimum-perimeter square-lattice patch with a Hamiltonian cycle for every even size, giving optimal-depth programmable circuits to implement Clifford states for all $n\,{=}\,4k{+}2$. Exhaustive and heuristic searches address the remaining cases for $n$ up to 256, and selected values up to 1,024 qubits. The improvement against comparable state-of-the-art, an LNN-compliant depth-$(2n{+}2)$ solution, is about 50\%. Finally, combining state synthesis circuits developed in this work with a known four-diagonal-stage decomposition gives rise to a depth $4n{-}4$ for $n\,{=}\,4k{+}2$ and depth $4n$ for $n\,{=}\,4k$ implementation of arbitrary Clifford unitaries. This improves the most relevant state-of-the-art, an LNN-compliant depth $7n{-}4$ construction, by about 43\%.

papers.title: Entanglement and Charge Transfer
papers.abstract: We compute the entropic order parameter introduced in (1905.10487) using the replica trick for two disjoint intervals. For a global symmetry, this quantity measures the mutual information carried by charge-anticharge intertwiners. We formulate the problem in terms of averages over twisted partition functions on replica Riemann surfaces, and obtain exact solutions for free fermions and compact bosons, for $U(1)$ symmetry and its discrete $\mathbb Z_N$ subgroups. We show that further averaging over both families of non-contractible cycles gives access to an additional quantity, which is the loss of Holevo information associated with complementary-charge measurements that occurs upon removing the intertwiners. For the boson, this quantity vanishes, whereas for Dirac fermions it equals the difference between the mutual information of the fermion-parity-gauged and ungauged theories, independently of the choice of even $\mathbb Z_N$ subgroup. Finally, we extend the analysis to non-Abelian symmetries using saddle expansions, deriving universal behavior in the nearly touching intervals limit and for a large number of fermions $N_F\gg1$.

papers.title: A Five-Dimensional Geometric Formulation of Geophysical Fluid Dynamics
papers.abstract: We apply a geometric formulation of Newtonian dynamics to inviscid compressible geophysical flow, with gravity and the effects of rotating or moving coordinates incorporated in the metric tensor. This construction relies on the introduction of an auxiliary fifth coordinate, which allows mass and momentum transport, internal energy, and pressure work to be combined into a single mass--momentum tensor. The covariant divergence of this tensor leads to the continuity equation for mass density, the three momentum equations, and the thermodynamic equation, with the system closed by an equation of state. A time-independent metric also yields conservation of total energy. We recover familiar forms of the equations and illustrate the construction in rotating spherical and terrain-following coordinates. The thin-shell and spherical-geopotential approximations, with constant effective gravity, simplify the metric while retaining vertical gravity and the traditional Coriolis terms. Emphasis is placed on the connection between the geometric structure of the formulation and the equations commonly used in atmospheric dynamics.
authors: St\'ephane Gaudreault, Seth Taylor, Arad Nasiri, Sanjeev S. Seahra, Raymond J. Spiteri

papers.title: Proxima: Optimizing Syndrome Extraction Circuit Scheduling for Practical Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.abstract: The fault-tolerant performance of quantum error correction codes relies critically on the scheduling of parity checks in syndrome extraction circuits (SECs). For general CSS-type quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, the vast scheduling space and intricate error-propagation patterns make it computationally prohibitive to directly optimize the logical error rate (LER) or the exact circuit-level distance ($d_{\mathrm{circ}}$). To address this challenge, we introduce Proxima, a highly effective automated SEC scheduling framework guided by a distance-related metric termed proximity. Defined directly on the detector error model (DEM), proximity quantifies the minimum number of additional faults required to complete a seed fault to an undetectable logical failure, naturally capturing arbitrary circuit-level fault mechanisms and bounding $d_{\mathrm{circ}}$ from above. Proxima synthesizes a pool of valid schedules at a target depth and ranks them by evaluating proximity within small, graph-local DEM fault subsets, progressively enlarging the subset only to break ties among top-ranked candidates. Across a broad spectrum of qLDPC code families, Proxima consistently attains low circuit depths and high circuit-level distance bounds, reducing LER by 1.4--2.6$\times$ over the strongest automated baseline and up to $40\times$ over others while generalizing robustly across noise models and decoders. Furthermore, by exploiting translational symmetry via a compact monomial representation, Proxima discovers depth-8 uniform schedules for bivariate bicycle codes that surpass even IBM's depth-7 reference schedule [Nature, 2024] by 2.1--5.1$\times$, establishing the DEM-level proximity as a practical objective for fault-tolerant compilation.
authors: Ruiyun Zhang, Guangqi Zhao, Zhaohui Yang, Yingjian Liu, Chenghong Zhu, Anbang Wu, Jun Xia, Yuan Xie

papers.title: Fixed Points as Programs: Finite Symmetry and One-Shot State-Gate Duality in the Misty-State Calculus
papers.abstract: The same quantum object can support several logically distinct descriptions: it can be an eigenstate of an operator, a fixed point of an action, a nonstabilizer resource, or a state consumed by a gate-injection protocol. We make these relations precise in the misty-state calculus. The semantic core is a normalized superposition constructor $x\star y=\operatorname{N}(x+y)$. For any finite unitary group $G$, whenever the orbit sum is nonzero, the normalized orbit cloud $\operatorname{N}(\sum_{g\in G}U_gx)$ is fixed by every element of $G$; the involutive specialization $x\star Ux$ is therefore a certified fixed-point constructor. Applied to $U=H$ and $x=|0\rangle$, it gives the nested misty state $M=\operatorname{N}\{W,\operatorname{N}\{W,B\}\}$, the $+1$ Hadamard eigenstate. This state is not a Pauli stabilizer state; it is an H-type magic state and is Clifford-equivalent to $T|+\rangle$. We then prove an exact one-shot state-gate duality. Writing $J=XZ$ and $R_\theta=e^{\theta J}$, the state $M_\theta=R_\theta|0\rangle$ can be consumed by a Clifford controlled-$J$ injection circuit to apply either $R_\theta$ or $R_\theta^{-1}$ to arbitrary data. Whenever $R_\theta^2$ is free, feed-forward makes the implementation deterministic. At $\theta=\pi/8$, $R_\theta^2=HZ=XH$ is Clifford, so one copy of $M$ implements one exact use of the non-Clifford gate $R=e^{\pi J/8}$; conversely one use of $R$ prepares $M$ from $|0\rangle$. We formulate this as a pair of sound semantic certificates, $\operatorname{Fix}(U)$ and $\operatorname{Prog}(R)$, and separate the resulting finite symmetrization mechanism from the genuinely recursive fixed-point role of the $Y$ combinator, while identifying the exact $S$-combinator sharing pattern in $x\star Ux$. The result is a small, auditable semantics in which invariance and consumable program resources coexist without being conflated.

papers.title: Thouless's bandwidth conjecture: a proof by elliptic periods
papers.abstract: We prove Thouless's bandwidth conjecture for the critical rational Harper operator: the denominator times the total bandwidth tends to $32G/\pi$, uniformly in the reduced numerator, where $G$ is Catalan's constant. We identify a universal limit of the normalized even coarea density. Positive real part and evenness give an integrable endpoint bound, so the local law determines the bandwidth. An exact finite-matrix formula reduces the local law to one normalized period for each fixed odd numerator. Explicit boundary polynomials, point blowups, and intersections determine a compact genus-one family. Nodal-annulus calculations fix its period equation and hence the universal density. An exact rational Fourier identity and uniform closed-path bounds extend the result to all reduced numerators and both denominator parities. The singular matrix limit, including its subtraction and normalization, is proved separately in detail.

papers.title: The Cost of Quantum State Conversion
papers.abstract: Which losses in quantum-state preparation can better control remove, and which are imposed by the available resources? We determine the least entropy production for converting known full-rank states using fresh thermal auxiliaries of fixed size and bounded energy range, with arbitrary driven joint control. For every reachable target, the asymptotic infimum is the decrease of a computable function of the state's spectrum. Explicit finite protocols approach this limit, including at saturated resource constraints. The result therefore supplies an attainable benchmark for state preparation, rather than only a lower bound. Reusable memory changes both reachability and the cost without enlarging any fresh auxiliary. A uniform memory gives an exact rescaling of the resource parameter; all memory states preparable from it under the same constraint have the same reachable targets and asymptotic costs. Externally supplied biased memories can do better, revealing a preparation resource distinct from dimension. With sufficient fixed memory, protocols reach exact product endpoints while dissipation decreases inversely with operation count. These results connect algorithmic cooling, quantum resource theories, and constructive control by separating unavoidable loss from the overhead of a chosen implementation.

papers.title: Quantum Loading of Charge and Spin-Adapted MPS
papers.abstract: Matrix product states (MPS) are powerful classical representations of correlated quantum states, but loading a large bond dimension MPS can substantially increase the cost in fault-tolerant quantum algorithms. We develop a circuit for preparing a U(1)~$\times$~SU(2)-symmetric MPS directly from spin-adapted reduced tensors. Using Householder--LKS synthesis, the circuit prepares each symmetry-allowed reduced block and applies Clebsch--Gordan coefficients to recover the magnetic degrees of freedom, avoiding explicit loading of the corresponding unfolded dense tensors. The reduced-tensor data loading is dominant in cost. We benchmark $4 \times 4$ and $4 \times 6$ Fermi--Hubbard states and active-space models of \ce{[Fe2S2]^2-}, \ce{[Fe4S4]^2-}, and low- and high-spin cytochrome P450. At 15-bit rotation precision, the molecular benchmarks show $\sim 14\times$ to $54\times$ Toffoli reductions, $\sim 20\times$ to $87\times$ active volume reduction, and $\sim 33\times$ to $140\times$ volume (Toffoli $\times$ qubits) reduction at the QROM-optimal point, relative to dense MPS loading. Fermi--Hubbard speedups increase with bond dimension and track the inverse tensor density, with modest qubit overhead. However, while we discuss generalization of our algorithm to reduce cost given further symmetry or using more performant unitary synthesis methods, extrapolation to larger lattices suggests that DMRG-state loading may exceed downstream phase-estimation costs, motivating co-design of state fidelity, compression, and the initial-state ansatz.
authors: Matthew R. Hennefarth, Lesley Gover, Carys Harvey, Zheting Jin, Ryan Levy, Sukin Sim, Modjtaba Shokrian Zini

papers.title: Quantum state texture from the average absolutes of density entries
papers.abstract: Quantum state texture is recently recognized as an important quantum resource in quantum information tasks. The only textureless state firstly proposed in $(Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 260801 (2024))$ is $f_1=\ket{f_1}\bra{f_1}$, \textcolor{red}{where $\ket{f_1}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\ket{i}$.} We take into account the modulus of the density matrix entries, and reasonably define the textureless states to be ones that all the modulus of the density matrix entries are equal. We present a quantifier of quantum state texture with respect to such non-convexity set of textureless states. As an application, we demonstrate in the transverse field Ising model that the texture of the subsystem of the ground state effectively characterize the quantum phase transitions, providing an alternative texture-based characterization of quantum criticality. We also provide the relationships among the quantum state texture, coherence and purity. Furthermore, we explore the quantum state texture based quantum speed limit in dissipative dynamical processes and derive the lower bound on the time required in texture variation for some dynamical processes.
authors: Cong Xu, Ming-Jing Zhao, Tao Li, Qing-Hua Zhang, Shao-Ming Fei

papers.title: Fate of chiral and $U(1)_A$ symmetries in hot QCD matter under background magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We summarize our recent lattice QCD study of chiral and singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking in background magnetic fields. The magnetic field explicitly reduces the non-singlet flavor symmetry through the unequal light-quark electric charges. We therefore study two neutral-channel susceptibility differences: $\chi_{\pi^0}-\chi_\sigma$ for chiral symmetry breaking and $\chi_{\pi^0}-\chi_{\delta^0}$ for singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking. The calculation uses fixed-scale $(2+1)$-flavor HISQ ensembles with $m_l=m_s^{\mathrm{phys}}/10$, corresponding to a zero-field pion mass of $M_\pi\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$. Magnetic fields enhance both susceptibility differences at low temperatures. Near the crossover, sufficiently strong fields instead suppress both differences. The suppression sets in at larger magnetic fields and is milder for the singlet-axial susceptibility difference than for the neutral chiral susceptibility difference.
authors: Dan Zhang, Heng-Tong Ding, Jos\'e Javier Hern\'andez Hern\'andez

papers.title: Algebraic instantons and non-Gaussian vacuum in quantum mechanics
papers.abstract: The standard instanton calculus in quantum mechanics is based on harmonic minima in the potential. When the perturbative vacuum is anharmonic, $V\simeq\lambda x^{2n}$ with $n\ge2$, the standard construction fails. We study this problem for a particle on a circle and subject to a potential $V(x)=16\lambda\sin^4(x/2)$. The instanton and its fluctuation operator are known in closed form, but they differ qualitatively from the familiar ones. Because $V''=0$ at the minimum, the classical vacuum is gapless, the instanton decays algebraically (an algebraic instanton), the zero mode is located at the threshold of a continuous spectrum, and the one-loop determinant is infrared divergent. Quantum mechanics generates a non-perturbative gap $E_q\propto\hbar^{4/3}\lambda^{1/3}$, and the instanton is embedded in a vacuum that is dynamically gapped, similar to what happens in Yang--Mills theory. We show that the one-instanton amplitude can be computed by matching the instanton trajectory to the exact vacuum part of the path integral. The resulting prefactor scales as $\hbar^{4/3}$, and this expression agrees with the numerical spectrum to a very high accuracy. The classical interaction between instantons decays as $T^{-3}$, whereas the correct result is an exponential decay controlled by the dynamically generated gap, beyond the quantum time scale. We provide an alternative derivation of this result based on a sum over intermediate states.
authors: Rahim Aziz, Hao Geng, Thomas Schaefer, Mithat \"Unsal

papers.title: Wilsonian renormalization group flow in QED with the Pauli term
papers.abstract:
We study the renormalization group (RG) flow of quantum electrodynamics (QED) with a Pauli term, $\kappa_	au\Bar{\psi}\sigma_{\mu
u}F_{\mu
u}\psi$, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG). In the GFERG, the gauge Ward--Takahashi identity takes the conventional form and is exactly preserved, and the gauge coupling flows only through the photon anomalous dimension~$\gamma_A$. In the leading large-$N_f$ approximation, the vacuum polarization induced by the Pauli coupling yields a nontrivial fixed point with~$e_*=0$, $\kappa_*
eq0$, and~$\gamma_A=-1$. This fixed point has three relevant directions, as does one of the fixed points of the asymptotically safe QED proposed by Gies and Ziebell. At finite~$N_f$, however, the $N_f$-independent one-loop effects on the fermion line, in particular the additive mass renormalization proportional to~$\kappa^2$, eliminate this fixed point unless $N_f$ is at least several tens; for~$N_f=1$ there is no fixed point at weak Pauli coupling. Along the full flow for~$N_f=1$, $\kappa_	au$ is irrelevant and is attracted to an induced value~$\kappa_{	ext{ind}}(e_	au)$, which is proportional to~$e_	au^3$ at weak coupling, while $e_	au^2$ is marginally irrelevant as in QED without the Pauli term.

papers.title: Compact Projected Pfaffian States for Rydberg-Blockaded Quantum Spin Systems
papers.abstract: We numerically demonstrate that a compact projected Pfaffian ansatz effectively describes the ground state of the nonintegrable PXP model. The variational wave function is obtained by applying separate Gutzwiller and Rydberg-blockade projectors to a general fermionic paired state, and each blockade-allowed configuration has an amplitude given by the Pfaffian of a configuration-selected pairing matrix. The exact blockade-projected product state of a known frustration-free deformation of the PXP model lies within the variational manifold and provides a physically motivated initial state for the variational Monte Carlo optimization toward the ground state of the pure PXP model. For a one-dimensional system of $N$ sites, optimizing all symmetry-allowed pairings in an $O(N)$-parameter wave function yields a near-exact ground state with a normalized energy variance (V-score) of order $10^{-9}$ despite the exponentially large blockade-constrained Hilbert space. On the square lattice, an $O(N)$-parameter wave function with the same amplitude structure yields relative energy errors below $0.2\%$ for clusters accessible to exact diagonalization and produces magnetizations consistent with available benchmarks. These results show that the same projected Pfaffian construction can be applied to blockade-constrained systems in both one and two dimensions.

papers.title: Exact environment checkpointing for memory-limited DMRG and TDVP
papers.abstract: Finite matrix-product-state sweep algorithms, such as the density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and the time-dependent variational principle (TDVP), store one environment tensor per site. At the bond dimensions needed for frustrated and two-dimensional systems this stack, rather than the state itself, exhausts the memory of the device. We adapt checkpointing to these sweeps: every $k$-th environment is kept, with $k\approx\sqrt{N}$ for $N$ sites, and the blocks in between are rebuilt when the sweep returns to them. The rebuild repeats the original contractions, so energies and states are reproduced bit for bit when the contractions are deterministic. Environment memory falls by 4.6-10x on cylinders of 96-384 sites. Bond-dimension searches with an implementation that rebuilds checkpoints at each half-sweep give gains of 1.77 for one level and 2.07 for two levels with eight contraction chunks on a single 141 GB GPU, using a 144-site triangular $J_1$-$J_2$ cylinder and stored baselines with matching chunking. Separate timings with checkpoints retained across half-sweeps give a one-level overhead of 6-15%, depending on the local eigensolver. At $D=1536$ the two-level schedule with eight chunks takes 1.42 times the sweep time of the equally chunked stored baseline, or 1.79 times that of the unchunked stored baseline. Simple models of the memory and the run time reproduce the measurements to within a few per cent. Unlike offloading, the method needs no host memory or disk, and the two can be combined. Implementations are provided for ITensorMPS.jl, TeNPy, MPSKit.jl and quimb.

papers.title: No complete set of mutually unbiased bases in C^6 without Fourier vanishing
papers.abstract: A recent exact certificate shows that C^6 admits no seven mutually unbiased bases, hence at most five (OpenAI, 2026). That argument has two parts. The first proves the Fourier-vanishing conjecture of Matolcsi, Ruzsa and Weiner for every complex Hadamard matrix of order six other than Tao's cubic matrix, and excludes the cubic matrix separately. The second feeds this vanishing into a positivity certificate on mixed moments of a hypothetical complete family. We show that the first part is not needed. We keep the same six families of test functions and the same linear identities, but we never set a moment to zero because of Fourier vanishing. New positive definite integer matrices still give the contradiction. The only inputs are orthonormality, unbiasedness, the second-moment (2-design) identity of a complete family, and the trivial bound |moment| <= 1. A standard-library program checks the certificate in exact integer and rational arithmetic in under a minute and a half. We also record computational observations that are not part of the proof: a systematic S_6-symmetric family of test functions appears to close the argument with relations of total order at most 7 instead of 11, and at order 9 two orbit types of test charges appear to suffice. In the prime-power dimensions 4,5,7,8, where complete families exist, the same pipeline finds no certificate, as it must.
authors: Jinze Yang, Yile Liu, Yangyang Li, Xiu-Hao Deng

papers.title: Efficient numerical measurement design and certified risk bounds for multiparameter quantum estimation
papers.abstract: Multiparameter quantum estimation requires efficient measurement design and reliable bounds on the attainable precision. We present Q-StARC, a numerical framework that combines measurement optimization with certified lower bounds on the weighted variance of locally unbiased estimators. The measurement search parameterizes rank-one measurements on a complex Stiefel manifold and combines projected ambient Adam updates, QR retraction, and Riemannian conjugate-gradient refinement. Independent risk bounds are obtained from a denominator-based matrix sum-of-squares hierarchy. When its support coefficients are optimized jointly, the hierarchy starts at the weighted Nagaoka-Hayashi (NH) bound and converges to the optimal locally unbiased risk, including for singular states. Numerical applications certify that the NH bound is unattainable for several finite-copy qubit models and two full eight-parameter qutrit models. For the qutrit examples, the certified relative gaps above the NH bound exceed $14\%$ and $11\%$, while the level-$m=1$ lower bounds agree with the best numerical measurement costs to relative differences of $4.5\times10^{-7}$ and $2.2\times10^{-6}$, respectively.

papers.title: Quantum state tomography with measurement-conditioned diffusion models
papers.abstract: We introduce Diff-QST, a measurement-conditioned diffusion model for quantum state tomography that learns from an ensemble of input states and reconstructs a physical density operator from noisy, possibly incomplete Pauli measurements in two or three denoising steps. In simulations of two to five qubits, Diff-QST has higher mean fidelity than maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) and a semidefinite-programming least-squares estimator (SDP) in all 120 tested conditions at nominal noise. After training, GPU reconstruction is faster than both in condition-averaged time at every system size and, at four and five qubits, in every condition. At four and five qubits, though not at two and three, Diff-QST also has higher fidelity than an architecture-matched regression baseline trained without diffusion. At five qubits, over the tested numbers of observables and shots per observable, it reaches a specified fidelity with 25%-67% fewer total shots than this baseline. Under state and noise distributions that differ from those used in training, Diff-QST retains its fidelity advantage over MLE and SDP in most tested conditions, although it can reverse. Diff-QST is therefore suited to fast tomography from noisy, incomplete Pauli measurements of states represented by its training ensemble.
authors: Woohyun Choi, Changsuk Noh, Changhyoup Lee

papers.title: A phase diagram for training and inference in language models
papers.abstract: A language model is a complex system whose behavior is determined jointly by the Transformer and the corpus, yet how the representation geometry in the Transformer relates to the actual behavior of language models remains open. We analyze how the representation geometry changes along the forward propagation of actual language models and characterize the representation geometry of a document at a given layer by two collective coordinates, document distinguishability and document dimension. On the phase diagram spanned by these collective coordinates, inference is represented as a flow along depth. We find that, for untrained models, depending on their initialization scale, most of the 156 inference flows move toward the collapse and noise regions of the phase diagram. By contrast, the inference flows of 8 trained models from 5 architecture families all enter and reside in the central region of the phase diagram. Describing the evolution of the flows with a discrete Langevin equation, we find that the difference between the inference flows of untrained runs and those of trained models reduces to whether the effective force on the flows in this region is of saddle or stable-node type. On Pythia-1.4B, we interpret the training process as a phase transition. These results give a unified gateway to the relation between representation geometry and language-model behavior.
authors: Zhuo-Yang Song, Zeyu Li, Qing-Hong Cao, Ming-xing Luo, Hua Xing Zhu

papers.title: Record-proof optical communication enabled by a quantum receiver with lossless optical decryption
papers.abstract: We propose record-proof physical-layer encryption (PLE) based on quantum-optimal reception. Unlike conventional symmetric-key encryption algorithms, the proposed scheme prevents decryption of recorded signals even if the secret key is disclosed after transmission. Existing PLE schemes rely on practical limitations of the eavesdropper's receiver in pursuing record-proof security; ours instead exploits the noncommutativity of conjugate optical quadratures to give the legitimate receiver an intrinsic sensitivity advantage. A phase-controlled Kennedy receiver performs lossless optical decryption and near-optimal binary-state discrimination. We demonstrate record-proof security with a 3.0-dB channel-loss budget, showing that quantum receivers offer cryptographic functions beyond sensitivity enhancement.
authors: Ken Tanizawa, Takayuki Kurosu, Fumio Futami, Kenji Nakahira, Kentaro Kato

papers.title: On $\iota$Quiver (BPS) Algebras and (Strict) Partitions
papers.abstract: We consider the $\iota$quiver algebras of split type associated with the quiver BPS algebras of affine type A. They are supposed to give twisted affine Yangians and (elliptic) $\iota$quantum toroidal algebras that could possibly arise from D-branes on $\mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{Z}_n$ with orientifolds. We mention some properties of these algebras, such as the minimalistic presentations in the rational cases and the coideal structures. We also investigate how one might identify these algebras from the quiver theories with orientifold actions. Moreover, we discuss some representations with combinatorial bases of these algebras. In particular, the algebras with $n=1,2$ in certain limits of the parameters have representations labelled by (coloured) strict/symmetric partitions, which in the case of $n=1$ recovers the known BPS counting of certain theories.

papers.title: Metallic or insulating magnetic phases of transition-metal oxides in light of the Slater vs Mott controversy
papers.abstract: Magnetic d-electron oxides usually have a long-range-ordered ground state and an above-ground-state disordered para phase. The historical Slater-Mott controversy still reverberating to date pertains to understanding the origin of the insulating vs metallic nature of these two phases. Slater suggested that the insulating character evolved from the long-range order (LRO) antiferromagnetic (AFM) cell-doubling, leading to energy band repulsion and thus to forming a band gap. The reliance on LRO to explain gapping suggests that the absence of LRO in the spin-disordered para-phase would deprive the system from band repulsion, thus predicting a metallic paramagnetic (PM) phase. This, however, conflicts with numerous current observations. The alternative Mott-Peierls-Hubbard view abandons the mean-field-like band structure view emphasizing instead the local interelectronic repulsion U as a strong correlation signature of gapping both at the presence or absence of LRO. However, U is not an easily measured or calculated quantity in periodic systems, a situation often leading in practice to treating U as an adjustable parameter. The current work uses a parameter-free mean-field-like approach (Density Functional Theory, DFT), allowing energy-lowering symmetry breaking. This is done by considering local magnetic motifs as building blocks of the macroscopic AFM or PM phases. It is found that even when such motifs are isolated electronically from each other (i.e. vanishing LRO) by embedding them in quantum barriers (such as magnetic NiO6 octahedra surrounded locally by wide-gap MgO) they exhibit an intrinsic band gap. Thus, the origin of the band gaps in AFM or PM phases need not be LRO or strong correlation and can be understood within the mean-field-like band structure approach with symmetry breaking.
authors: Xiuwen Zhang, Jia-Xin Xiong, Alex Zunger

papers.title: Basic introduction to Freidlin-Wentzell theory
papers.abstract: Freidlin-Wentzell theory provides the quantitative foundation for rare, noise-induced transitions in stochastic dynamical systems, predicting optimal transition pathways, the exponential scaling of mean escape times, and the long-term occupancy of competing attractors in metastable systems. Here we present a pedagogical, physics-oriented review built around a unified Hamiltonian framework: starting from the infinitesimal generator of a continuous-time Markov process, we derive the local Hamiltonian, obtain the Lagrangian and action functional via Legendre-Fenchel duality, and construct the quasi-potential landscape. We apply this streamlined formalism across weak-noise diffusions, Markov jump processes, weakly interacting particle ensembles, and nonequilibrium stochastic fields, alongside exact conditions for macroscopic coarse-graining. Along the way, we highlight how broken detailed balance drives forward and reverse transition paths apart, explain where local linear stability and Gaussian approximations break down, and assemble multi-attractor landscapes using combinatorial $W$-graphs. Finally, we bridge the analytical theory to modern numerical solvers, including ordered upwind methods, geometric minimum action algorithms, and neural-network parameterizations, and provide an accompanying GPU-accelerated Python package.

papers.title: Bowed-String-Mechanism-Inspired Quantum Dissociation Control of Molecules
papers.abstract: Inspired by Guettler's mechanics of accelerating Helmholtz motion, we present a predictive laser pulse-shaping strategy to rapidly initiate the multiphoton dissociation of vibrationally excited diatomic molecules. In intense infrared fields, NO molecules often exhibit unpredictable control windows due to the chaotic fragmentation of intensity thresholds. By incorporating a bowing-analogue transient shaper enforced by a boundary-matching constraint with symmetric derivative slope transitions and vanishing initial boundary conditions ($T(0) = 0, T'(0) = 0$), we demonstrate that a pulse engineered with non-linear front-flank acceleration reduces the multi-valued threshold topology into a single, predictable linear dissociation corridor. Wigner quasiprobability distributions confirm that this temporal acceleration trajectory opens cantori bottlenecks and suppresses wave-packet fragmentation, restricting the quantum non-classicality index to $M_{\text{nc}} \le 0.15$. Our simulations verify that this trajectory engineering preserves wave-packet localization and maintains high dissociation yields ($P_{\text{diss}} > 0.95$) even under Markovian thermal dephasing ($\delta/\omega_0 = 10^{-4}$) and frozen rotational variations up to $J = 5$. Comparison with contemporary ultrafast spectral phase modulation protocols demonstrates that conventional smooth pulse envelopes, despite advanced phase-chirping, exhibit limitations in restricting non-hyperbolic cantori stickiness due to insufficient sub-picosecond acceleration. In contrast, our boundary-constrained shaper enforces a deterministic, single-valued dissociation corridor under equivalent few-picosecond control windows.

papers.title: Deterministic preparation of squeezed Schr\"odinger cat states with arbitrary size and squeezing
papers.abstract: We introduce a scheme for the deterministic preparation of squeezed Schr\"odinger cat states based on reservoir engineering. Our proposal relies on the linear and quadratic coupling of an oscillator mode to an auxiliary mode that decays into a vacuum reservoir. For suitable couplings, we show that the system unconditionally relaxes into a pure steady state. We derive an analytical expression for the steady state in terms of the coupling constants, and show that it corresponds to a displaced and squeezed finite superposition of Fock states. Numerical simulations further confirms that this state is reached with unit fidelity from a thermal initial state, without measurement, feedback or post-selection. Additionally, we derive analytical expressions for the non-Gaussianity and the Wigner function of the steady state. Our results reveal that states exhibiting maximal non-Gaussianity are excellent approximations of squeezed Schr\"odinger cat states, with fidelities exceeding $0.996$. The optimal squeezing stays close to 3dB, while the squared cat size scales proportionally with the highest Fock state occupation number in the finite superposition of the steady state. These maximally non-Gaussian states also maximise the Wigner logarithmic negativity. Finally, by selecting the appropriate ratios of the couplings, our scheme can generate cat states subject to arbitrary squeezing and displacement.

papers.title: Spectral Moments of the Projected Hubbard Configuration Graph: Connectivity, Exchange, and Virtual Doublons
papers.abstract: At strong on-site repulsion, the lowest band of $n$ lattice fermions is the spectrum of the hopping projected onto configurations without double occupancy, $H_\infty=P_0H_tP_0$. We study its moments, for few fermions in the square-lattice Hubbard model and, where the arguments allow, on any finite graph. (1) For spin-independent Hermitian hopping (no on-site terms) on any $N\geq2$-site graph, $\mu_2=\frac{n(N-n)}{N(N-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}|t_{ij}|^2$, for any spin composition. (2) On any finite graph, $\mu_4$ is exactly linear in the same-spin pair count, as four hops permute particles by at most a transposition or 3-cycle; for uniform hopping on a simple graph with $N\geq4$ the slope is $\alpha(N,n)=-8C_4(N-n)(8N-11n-2)/[N(N-1)(N-2)(N-3)]$, fixed by the number $C_4$ of 4-cycles. (3) At large finite $U$, the second-order Schrieffer-Wolff correction is Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal to $H_\infty$ on every triangle-free graph, so the band variance has no $1/U$ term; its $U^{-2}$ coefficient, an exact trace checked by exact diagonalization, is negative at the low fillings computed. (4) Under a Peierls flux, the exchange slope $\alpha(N,2,\Phi)=-\frac{64}{N-1}\cos\Phi_\square$ ($L\times L$ tori, $L=3$ or $L\geq5$) carries the ordinary charge-$e$ harmonic, while the doublon (bound-pair) hopping acquires a doubled phase, $t_de^{2iA_{ij}}$: the second-order single-doublon Hamiltonian is exactly $\pi$-periodic ($h/2e$) under a boundary twist, and the exact two-electron U-band follows numerically, up to $O((2\lambda)^L/U^{L-1})$. Result (1), the permutation bound, the orthogonality in (3) and the doubled phase are machine-checked in Lean 4. Repulsive binding and the pair charge $2e$ are known; new are the exact moment structure and the derivation of the doubled phase. We make no claim about many-pair phase stiffness, off-diagonal long-range order or superconductivity.

papers.title: Quasinormal Modes and Environmental Trapping around Charged Letelier Black Holes with Perfect-Fluid Dark Matter and Quintessence
papers.abstract: We compute the massless scalar quasinormal spectra of charged Letelier black holes surrounded by logarithmic perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) and quintessence, for $\Lambda=0$ and for asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes, together with the test Maxwell spectra for $\Lambda=0$. For $\Lambda=0$, sixth order WKB values with Pad\'e resummation agree with independent time domain evolutions to within $0.06\%$ for the fundamental modes. Stronger string cloud and quintessence lower both the oscillation frequencies and the damping rates, while a larger charge or a larger positive PFDM parameter $\beta$ raises both. In our convention $\beta>0$ means negative PFDM energy density; negative $\beta$ gives a positive density and reverses the shift. The angular frequency and Lyapunov exponent of the unstable circular null orbit reproduce the eikonal trends and approximate the $\ell=2$ WKB frequencies at the percent level. For $\Lambda<0$ the scalar potential diverges at the AdS boundary and the single barrier WKB formula does not apply. We therefore solve the eigenvalue problem with a Chebyshev pseudospectral method in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates, with regularity at the horizon and a Dirichlet condition at the boundary, and check the modes against time domain evolutions and Schwarzschild-AdS benchmarks. The AdS spectrum contains long-lived modes trapped between the photon sphere barrier and the reflecting boundary, with damping rates spanning about five orders of magnitude. The damping correlates with the ratio of the oscillation frequency to the barrier top frequency, consistent with leakage through the barrier. No growing modes are found in the test field sectors and parameter ranges studied, which does not establish the stability of the fully coupled system.
authors: Semra Gurtas Dogan, Abdullah Guvendi, Hassan Hassanabadi

papers.title: Character variety of the punctured sphere and the determinantal variety
papers.abstract: We show that the SL(2;C) character variety of the n-punctured sphere is described via the determinantal variety defined by an n x n symmetric matrix of rank at most 4 whose entries are the traces of simple closed curves on the surface. This result generalizes the Fricke-Klein-Vogt relations to arbitrary n, and we determine the structure of the kernel of the associated matrix.

papers.title: Towards a foundation model for Type IIB flux vacua
papers.abstract: Progress in characterising the Type IIB flux landscape requires scalable methods for constructing flux vacua. In this work, we investigate generative models as a framework for sampling vacua across multiple Calabi-Yau geometries and for directing searches towards specified physical properties. We compare transformers and diffusion models trained to generate quantised fluxes together with approximate values of the complex structure moduli and axio-dilaton. We exploit a staged training procedure comprising pre-training, and post-training via reinforcement learning, and assess how each stage improves the generated distributions and enables targeted sampling. We further examine whether structures learned from geometries with smaller $h^{1,2}$ can be transferred to geometries with larger $h^{1,2}$ through fine-tuning on specialised datasets. Our results provide evidence that generative models can learn distributions of flux vacua across distinct compactifications, improve searches for vacua with selected properties and transfer information between geometries. This establishes a concrete basis for developing a foundation model of the Type IIB flux landscape.
authors: Sven Krippendorf, Magdalena Larfors, Zhimei Liu, Andreas Schachner, Moritz Walden

papers.title: Neumann zero modes and the locality of the derivative expansion
papers.abstract: The derivative expansion (DE) provides a useful approximation to the Casimir interaction energy between two close surfaces. It has the form of a local functional, obtained from a zero momentum expansion. However, when the system involves a massless field satisfying Neumann conditions, that expansion may develop nonanalytic terms. We present here a study on how this property reflects itself in the need to add to the DE some novel, nonlocal terms. These are, we argue, akin to the ones introduced in effective theories because of the presence of massless particles in loops. We pinpoint the mode responsible for this effect, and construct the effective action due to its fluctuations, showing that it reproduces known nonanalytic contributions, and present the corresponding nonlocal addition to the DE. We also predict a new nonanalyticity: Neumann conditions in $3+1$ dimensions at zero temperature produce a term of order $|{\mathbf k}_\shortparallel |^3$, with a parameter-free coefficient, between the (local) second and fourth orders of the expansion. We show that, for a cylinder in front of a plane, the zero-mode loop adds to the local expansion a term of relative order $(L/R)^{3/2}$, with a coefficient that we compute explicitly, showing that it accounts for the behaviour of the existing numerical fits for that geometry.
authors: C. D. Fosco, F. D. Mazzitelli

papers.title: Quantum teleportation with photons from remote quantum dots emitting at telecom C-band
papers.abstract: Employing quantum teleportation to increase the communication distance in quantum channels requires distinct quantum light sources, preferably operating at telecommunication wavelength. Here we utilize two semiconductor In(Ga)As quantum dots, strain engineered to emit in the telecom C-band, as sources of single- and entangled-photons, respectively. This enables a full-photonic quantum teleportation experiment, achieving a maximum teleportation fidelity of 92.7(5)%. Owing to state-of-the-art source brightness, and high time resolution, it is here possible to employ the three-photon coincidences to fully quantify the time-dependence of the process. In this way, we highlight current limitations and implement an optimization in the data-processing which leads to the maximization of achievable teleportation fidelity and coincidence rates. These results constitute a step forward in practical implementations of quantum teleportation in future fiber-based quantum networks.
authors: Raphael Joos, Michelle Pfahl, Ponraj Vijayan, Michal Vyvlecka, Michael Jetter, Simone L. Portalupi, Peter Michler

papers.title: Pulse-timing errors in exchange-only spin qubits: how one control imperfection propagates to VQE, QAOA and fault-tolerance primitives
papers.abstract: In an exchange-only (EO) spin qubit every gate is a sequence of Heisenberg exchange pulses whose only continuous parameter is the pulse area. We ask how an error in that area propagates to an algorithm's result. On up to six encoded qubits we compile VQE for H$_2$ and LiH, QAOA MaxCut, Grover search, phase estimation and a distance-3 repetition code into exchange pulses and perturb every pulse with a systematic fractional error $\varepsilon$, an offset or per-pulse jitter. For circuits whose first-order response is negligible at the threshold, the useful regime ends at $\varepsilon$ of a few $10^{-3}$: chemical accuracy is lost at $\approx6\times10^{-3}$ for both molecules and 5% of success probability between 3 and $9\times10^{-3}$ for 498-1216 pulses. A systematic error accumulates as the square of the depth and biases the answer; jitter accumulates linearly and, within statistics, does not bias phase estimation. Leakage from inter-block pulses is a third of the CNOT error, survives variational re-optimisation and a leakage-controlled entangler, and makes a leakage-blind repetition-code round worse than its uncorrected data by a factor 38-93 at $\varepsilon=10^{-2}$ in three of four compilations; in the fourth the uncorrected data already fail. The compilation moves the thresholds by a factor of two to eight. Measured over-rotation and exchange noise put devices at the edge of this regime, and with the measured 3.5 $\mu$s $T_2^*$ a quasi-static magnetic gradient limits thousand-pulse circuits unless $J/h$ reaches several hundred MHz with continuous areas, because a duration grid of 2-5% of the SWAP time starts to cost chemical accuracy. As a bit budget, a common-mode area error needs 8-10 significant bits and a 6-bit significand for the durations suffices in the tested circuits; half-precision words and picosecond timers exceed this; older devices had 6-8 bits of analog stability.

papers.title: Unstable Periodic Orbit Localization in a Nonlinear System-Environment Model
papers.abstract: The role of unstable periodic orbits (UPOs) is investigated in the chaotic dynamics of a nonlinear system-environment model composed of a central two-level system coupled to an environment of two-level systems. Families of UPOs embedded in chaotic regions are identified and their local instability is characterized. Their behavior is examined under variations of the environment size, energy, and system symmetry, allowing the model to serve as a controlled testbed in which the dimensionality and dynamical conditions can be systematically modified. Characteristic UPO-based dynamical quantities are used to assess the influence of these periodic orbits on nearby chaotic trajectories, including occupation of the UPO tube, its persistence at late times, return fidelity enhancement, and recurrence timing. Across the different model variations considered, trajectories initialized close to the UPOs retain statistically detectable spatial and temporal signatures associated with the periodic orbits. These results indicate that unstable periodic orbits can retain a measurable organizing influence on surrounding chaotic trajectories across changes in dimensionality, energy, and system symmetry, giving rise to scar-like dynamical signatures in a simple nonlinear system--environment model.

papers.title: Efficient AOD-Transport Compilation for Neutral-Atom Arrays
papers.abstract: Neutral-atom quantum computers execute two-qubit gates by shuttling atoms between storage and entanglement zones with acousto-optic deflectors (AODs). The efficiency of these movements determines circuit fidelity via transport overhead, idle-atom crosstalk, and atom-transfer errors. Additionally, AOD hardware constraints limit parallel atom movements, so efficient qubit placement and routing are essential. We present NEAT (Neutral-atom Efficient AOD-Transport compiler). Its transport-informed placement evaluates each decision by its incremental equivalent time, a single cost combining transport time, atom-transfer loss, and crosstalk. Its partial-progress routing allows conflicting moves to advance concurrently via intermediate waypoints. NEAT also schedules gates to maximize parallelism and uses a staggered atom array whose trap geometry preemptively avoids AOD violations without extra moves. On standard benchmark circuits, NEAT outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) compilers in fidelity, circuit duration, and compilation time. On scalability benchmarks of up to 1,000 qubits, it shortens circuits by 1.9x, reduces the negative log-fidelity by 1.5x, and compiles 6.6x faster than SOTA compilers on average. Overall, NEAT is a lightweight yet effective compiler for efficient and scalable neutral-atom quantum computing. The code is available at https://github.com/HaydnCheng77/NEAT.

papers.title: Self-assembly of dipolar nanoclusters on an attractive substrate: A coarse-grained simulation approach
papers.abstract: Recently, Thomas et al. [Nanoscale 17, 18291 (2025)] showed that bismuth oxido nanoclusters (BiO-NCs) of the type [Bi$_{38}$ O$_{45}$ (Boc-L-Phe-O)$_{24}$] form chains when deposited onto gold or pyrolitic graphite substrates. This chain formation is significantly enhanced when the bismuth in the BiO-NCs is partially replaced by cerium through doping. In this work, we study a simplified, coarse-grained model of this process, namely (magnetic) Stockmayer particles in the presence of an attractive substrate. The model is investigated by means of molecular dynamics simulations. The deposition experiment is mimicked by a rapid quench from high temperature to a low temperature below the bulk coexistence curve. The results are found to be qualitatively similar to the experimental observations reported earlier. In our simulations, we find significant chain formation in the bulk even at rather low concentrations, which is in contrast to the BiO-NCs in ethanol for which dynamic light scattering reveals negligible aggregation in the absence of the substrate. This lends support to a scenario, conjectured in the work of Thomas at al., where the dipole moments are induced by the particle-substrate interaction and hence there is little dipole moment in the bulk. In a second part, we study the system in equilibrium. We consider the scaling of chains, the number of layers populated as a function of two-dimensional density, and we draw analogies to polymers on interfaces, which have been extensively studied over the past decades. Most notably, it is found that the chains behave as self-avoiding walks at low densities, which gives way to rod-like scaling at higher densities.
authors: Denis Gessert, Harshita Chauhan, Thi Ngoc Ha Nguyen, Christoph Tegenkamp, Michael Mehring, Varsha Banerjee, Martin Weigel

papers.title: The topological degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system
papers.abstract: We resolve the long-standing open problem of computing the Leray--Schauder degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system on a closed oriented surface $M$. If $d_{m,k}$ denotes the degree in the block $(4\pi m,4\pi(m+1))\times(4\pi k,4\pi(k+1))$, then \[ \sum_{m,k\geq0}d_{m,k}x^my^k =(1-x)^{\chi(M)-1}(1-y)^{\chi(M)-1}(1-xy)^{\chi(M)}, \] where $\chi(M)$ is the Euler characteristic of $M$. Nonvanishing of $d_{m,k}$ thus gives an existence criterion in terms of the topology of $M$ and the parameter block. At each step of the degree computation, we show that the only possible local mass pairs are $(4\pi,0)$ and $(8\pi,4\pi)$. We use generic perturbations and local second-order information on the weights to exclude collisions of shadow centers and splitting at mixed blow-up points. The shadow degrees and the Morse index then give the degree jump at each critical value.
authors: Youngae Lee, Haoyu Li, Juncheng Wei, Wen Yang, Lei Zhang

papers.title: Polarization waves in open-barrier quantum-dot cellular automata
papers.abstract: Quantum-dot cellular automata (QCA) are almost always operated as bistable digital logic. We develop a closed-form theory of small-signal polarization waves in the open-barrier regime, where tunnelling within each cell is comparable to or stronger than the electrostatic kink coupling between cells, so that a line of cells responds linearly instead of latching. Linearizing the coherence-vector equations of the intercellular Hartree approximation (ICHA) about the unpolarized state gives a lattice dispersion with a low-frequency cutoff, an evanescent band below it and a Klein-Gordon long-wavelength limit, and relaxation toward the instantaneous equilibrium damps the waves at a rate that depends on the wavenumber. The exact Jordan-Wigner solution and exact diagonalization confirm the mode as a sharp quasiparticle, with ICHA frequencies within 6% of the exact ones once the tunnelling energy is at least twice the kink energy, and show that the exact chain also carries waves over a range of couplings where the ICHA predicts latching. A leading low-temperature estimate of thermal dephasing sets a ceiling on the operating temperature of about 13.6 K per terahertz of gap for a carrier that keeps its phase over 30 periods. At junctions the waves scatter through a lattice scattering matrix that reaches the familiar transmission-line value only at mid-band.

papers.title: Hardware-Aware Realization of Deterministic Quantum-Walk Search on Complete Bipartite Graphs
papers.abstract: Complete bipartite graphs offer a canonical platform for deterministic quantum search with quadratic speedup. We report the first experimental realization of deterministic discrete-time quantum-walk search over complete bipartite graphs, enabled by high-fidelity operations and a dynamical-phase compensation scheme, using a digital gate-based processor rather than an evolution-based platform. By compiling the search circuits to the native gate set and square-lattice topology, we implement full-space encoding to realize instances of graph sizes $N = 4$ and $8$, with success probabilities of 97.6% and 70.8% for finding the marked vertex, respectively. We also realize resource-efficient exact instances up to size $N = 16$, the largest achieving 66% success probability. Separately, a reduced invariant-subspace encoding preserves the dynamics of the deterministic search algorithm on two qubits for nominal problem sizes up to $N = 256$, with the success probability approaching 50%. Resource analyses of logical, hardware-compiled, and fault-tolerant-gate-set-synthesized circuits show that circuit depth and size scale as $\sqrt{N}$, with hardware overheads entering only as constant prefactors. For application-scale graphs ($N \sim 10^5$), an effective gate-fidelity model requires per-gate infidelity near $10^{-7}$. These results establish a concrete algorithm-to-hardware pathway for deterministic structured quantum search on gate-based quantum processors.
authors: Tao Rong, Meng Li, Xin Tong, Jianbin Cai, Yu Li, Naibin Zhou, Shaowei Li, Sirui Cao, Yuan Li, Yu Xu, Fusheng Chen, Ming Gong, Xiaoming Sun, Chen Zha

papers.title: Matrix Star-Triangle Relations
papers.abstract: We propose a matrix generalization of the star--triangle relations and identify solutions underlying the $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ chiral Potts models.

papers.title: Imperfect Cavities Select Better: Enantioselectivity Beyond Pure Helicity
papers.abstract: Single-handed light appears ideally suited to select a preferred handedness of matter. For chiral molecules in a cavity, we show that this intuition fails. Hybridization of light and matter reshapes the optical resonance through a self-energy that mixes opposite helicities. As a result, the difference in power absorbed by opposite enantiomers is generically maximized by light of mixed, rather than pure, helicity. We clarify why chiral selection admits such mixed-helicity optima in more general light--matter systems. For a concrete set of cavity modes, we find that molecular localization at a weak helicity bias considerably outperforms helically pure designs, thus identifying spatial control as a promising design direction for devices previously thought to be ``imperfect''.

papers.title: Readout errors limit how far adaptive quantum circuits can entangle
papers.abstract: Measurement and feedforward let quantum circuits entangle arbitrarily distant qubits in constant depth if measurement records are perfect and classical communication is instantaneous. We allow each reported bit to flip independently with a fixed probability between zero and one half, keeping all gates ideal. Consider a square-lattice device with a unique path between the endpoints and a bounded number of qubits per site. Beyond $\exp[O(D^3)]$ steps along that path, every depth-$D$ circuit starting from a product state leaves the endpoints exactly separable in every record, however rare. By copying outcomes onto spare qubits beside the path before readout, we attain a reach of $\exp[\Theta(D^3)]$ for a nondestructive parity measurement at fixed accuracy without postselection. On a one-dimensional chain, the optimal reach for the same measurement is $\exp[\Theta(D^2)]$. On any interaction graph, a constant-depth circuit starting from a product state needs $\Omega(L\ln L)$ qubits to entangle endpoints at graph distance $L$. The reliability of local readout thus limits the depth advantage of adaptive circuits for long-range entanglement.

papers.title: On reflection positivity of lattice chiral fermions
papers.abstract: We point out that the overlap Weyl fermion, the spacetime lattice realization of a Weyl fermion underlying L\"uscher's construction of lattice chiral gauge theories, is not reflection positive in two and four dimensions at finite lattice spacing. Consequently, the standard Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction does not yield a Hilbert space with a self-adjoint Hamiltonian. In two dimensions, we further show that the overlap Weyl fermion cannot be cut open: the lattice action becomes nonlocal in the presence of a boundary, as expected from the gravitational anomaly of the continuum field theory. By contrast, the overlap Dirac fermion is known to be reflection positive. However, its compact axial symmetry is not invariant under the reflection, whereas a reflection-invariant axial symmetry is noncompact, and both are part of an Onsager algebra.

papers.title: Equivariant Localization with Electric Monodromy in M-theory
papers.abstract: We extend equivariant localization for supersymmetric AdS$_3$ backgrounds of M-theory to solutions with nonzero electric flux periods. The associated local electric potential acquires additive monodromy, contributing to the warped volume alongside R-symmetry fixed points and outer boundaries. Using Killing-spinor identities, we relate the electric periods to magnetic flux and, for a class of compact backgrounds, the warped volume to the electric Maxwell charge. We also derive a relation between the gravitational anomaly and the electric flux. We apply these results to AdS$_3$ $\times S^3 \times S^3 \times T^2$ and AdS$_3$ $\times S^3 \times K3 \times S^1$, recovering their central charges and deriving the R-current levels of the former directly from eleven-dimensional supergravity. Finally, we study a noncompact half-BPS AdS$_3$ $\times S^3\times S^3$ geometry fibered over a periodic half-cylinder, where fixed-point, monodromy and outer-boundary contributions coexist.

papers.title: A Forward Bit Makes Error Correction Dispensable for Antidegradable Amplitude-Damping Channels
papers.abstract: Preserving a qubit usually relies on redundant encoding over many uses of a noisy channel. We prove that for antidegradable amplitude damping, one channel use with one forward classical bit matches or beats every forward-assisted or unassisted code with any number of uses. We then show that variational circuits learn to switch from error correction to classical assistance as damping grows, beating a dual-certified bound on all unassisted three-use codes and, relative to the best unassisted see-saw, extending storage time by up to 13% at entanglement fidelity down to 0.65.
authors: Ahmed Gamal, Yasutaka Wada, Walid Gomaa, Norhan El-Sayed, Keiji Kimura, Salem F. Hegazy, Kazunori Ueda, Ahmed El-Mahdy

papers.title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
papers.abstract: We exhibit a complex Hadamard matrix of nonzero defect which is isolated among complex Hadamard matrices, up to Hadamard equivalence. This counterexample is realized by a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of size $13$, with entries roots of order $6$ of unity. In the language of commuting squares, this shows that the span condition, previously introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation, is not a necessary condition for isolation.

papers.title: Generative Models using Multi-layer Quantum Extreme Learning Machines
papers.abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) and the closely related quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) paradigm exploit the complex dynamics of an uncontrolled quantum system for machine learning, offering an alternative to variational quantum algorithms whose training is hindered by barren plateaus and costly circuit optimization. Because the quantum system itself is left fixed, learning reduces to fitting a linear readout of a set of measured observables, and no gradient is ever taken through the quantum device. In this work we repurpose this paradigm for generative modeling: a fixed, randomly initialized multi-layer QELM transforms a scalar latent variable into a rich vector of measured expectation values, and only a simple linear readout is trained to map these to samples of a target distribution. The readout is fitted by minimizing the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) between generated and target samples. We show that this algorithm is capable of reproducing a range of one- and two-dimensional distributions. Moreover, encoding the class label on dedicated qubits enables conditional generation of different classes of distributions with the same linear readout. We show that this cannot be achieved by the linear readout alone, and that the reservoir dynamics play a role in the ability to distinguish the different classes of distributions. We also show that using a simple six-qubit reservoir one is able to generate handwritten digits from the Digits and MNIST datasets with high accuracy. Moreover, replacing the Haar-random dynamics by time evolution under several physical Hamiltonians leaves the performance unchanged, provided the evolution spreads the input across the register. Finally, we show that a classical random Fourier feature model of the same size performs equally well: at the sizes we study, the QELM offers no advantage over its classical counterpart.
authors: Amir Azzam, M. Pilar Casado, Michele Grossi, Arnau Riera, Sofia Vallecorsa

papers.title: HVP contributions to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in spacelike and timelike domains
papers.abstract: The hadronic vacuum polarization contributions to the muon anomalous magnetic moment $a^{\text{HVP}}_{\mu}$ in spacelike and timelike domains are recapped. The values of $a^{\text{HVP}}_{\mu}$ assessed within dispersively-improved perturbation theory are reported. The obtained results can be employed in the evaluations of $a^{\text{HVP}}_{\mu}$ in the framework of such methods as lattice studies, MUonE project, and others.

papers.title: Mixed-state topological transitions with hidden long-range correlations
papers.abstract: We study a decoherence-driven transition from a one-dimensional symmetry-protected topological state to a trivial product state. The decoherence acts onsite while preserving the protecting symmetry on average. Although conventional local correlations remain short-ranged across the transition, we uncover hidden nondecaying long-range correlations in a symmetry-twisted ensemble that weights states according to their symmetry charge. At the transition, the twisted correlation length diverges and the twisted partition function becomes singular. These signatures can be directly extracted from symmetry-resolved measurement outcomes, making the hidden critical behavior accessible on current quantum platforms at mesoscopic system sizes. We demonstrate this through numerical simulations of the measurement process.
authors: Ze-Min Huang, Frank Pollmann, Sebastian Diehl

papers.title: On Thermodynamics of AdS Black Holes in Square-Root Nonlinear Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: Inspired by exponential Maxwell models, we propose a new black hole solution in square root nonlinear electrodynamics. Using the analogy between black hole mechanics and thermodynamics, we investigate the corresponding stability, the P-v criticality and the phase transitions. As a result, we find that the obtained black hole exhibits Van der Waals behaviors without additional corrections which typically appear in universal ratio computations.
authors: A. Belhaj, S. E. Ennadifi, M. Jemri, M. Nach

papers.title: Casimir-like wormholes
papers.abstract: We investigate spherically symmetric spacetimes sourced by matter with energy density $\rho \propto 1/r^{4}$ and equation of state $p_r = \omega \rho$. We derive the most general solution of Einstein's equations for this class of sources, obtaining black holes, naked singularities and traversable wormholes, parametrized by the integration constants and $\omega$. We show that only two classes of matter can support traversable wormholes: Casimir-type matter with $\omega > 0$ and phantom matter with $\omega < -1$, while quintessence and conventional dark energy are excluded by the flare-out condition. For the Casimir value $\omega = 3$, the transverse pressure approaches $p_t \to -\rho$ near the central singularity, so the full algebraic structure of the Casimir stress-energy tensor, $\rho \propto -1/r^{4}$, $p_r = 3\rho$, $p_t = -\rho$, is not imposed but emerges from Einstein's equations. Treating the amplitude of the energy density as a free classical parameter, we obtain wormholes with throat radii from microscopic to astrophysical scales. These Casimir-like configurations share the functional form of the Casimir tensor but are not generated by the physical Casimir effect; Garattini's Planck-scale Casimir wormhole is recovered when the quantum Casimir energy scale is imposed. The total amount of exotic matter is finite for arbitrary $\omega$ and scales linearly with the throat radius. Analyzing the traveler's acceleration, tidal forces and transit times, we show that radial free fall satisfies all human traversability conditions for $r_0 \gtrsim 10^{8}$ m. Finally, embedding diagrams illustrate three geometric regimes depending on $\omega$.

papers.title: Canonical partition function and equation of state in the heavy quark region of finite-density lattice gauge theory
papers.abstract: We investigate the phase structure and equations of state in lattice gauge theory at finite temperature and finite density, focusing on the canonical partition function obtained by decomposing the grand partition function with respect to particle number. We demonstrate that when quark masses are heavy, the complex phase of the quark determinant, which causes the sign problem, can be controlled by decomposing the grand partition function according to particle number. In this study, we propose an algorithm to calculate the canonical partition function for heavy-quark, high-density effective theory and test it for the first time using one-flavor $SU(2)$ gauge theory, a case where the sign problem arises. When the grand partition function of $SU(2)$ is decomposed into canonical partition functions, the sign problem is serious in odd-particle sectors, while it is mild in even-particle sectors. The odd-particle sectors also expose a fundamental issue: center symmetry makes the canonical partition function of $SU(N_c)$ vanish unless the particle number is an integer multiple of $N_c$. Although appropriate in the confinement phase, this restriction must be treated carefully in the deconfinement phase. We resolve the issue by introducing an infinitesimal external field, calculate the canonical partition functions by Monte Carlo simulation, reconstruct the grand partition function, and determine thermodynamic observables over a wide range of temperature and density. Furthermore, we find that the chemical-potential dependence of the equation of state at low temperatures exhibits behavior characteristic of the hadron resonance gas model, and that no softening of the QCD matter occurs at finite density.
authors: Shinji Ejiri, Hideya Hashizume, Masanari Koiida

papers.title: Radar Waveform Design via Convex Semidefinite Relaxation
papers.abstract: The ambiguity function (AF) of a radar waveform describes its ability to resolve targets in range and Doppler. Designing a waveform that attains a prescribed AF magnitude is a phase retrieval problem with four trivial ambiguities, and a time- or band-limited pulse is determined up to these ambiguities by at most three times as many AF samples as it has time samples or frequencies. Existing solvers for the narrowband AF, however, are non-convex: they cannot guarantee that they reach the global minimizer, which is unique only up to the trivial ambiguities, so the recovered pulse depends on the starting point. This letter addresses this gap by lifting the problem to positive semidefinite matrices supported on the pulse band, where each AF sample becomes the magnitude of a linear functional. In the lifted space, recovery is formulated as a convex program, and a dual certificate provides a sufficient condition for exactness. The proposed algorithm, wavex, combines an initialization by relaxed reflections, convex semidefinite surrogate steps, and a local polish. Numerical experiments show that wavex accurately recovers band-limited pulses from complete AFs and from AFs with most of their samples removed, provided the remaining samples determine the pulse, and that its accuracy degrades gracefully as the noise increases. wavex is built on the open-source library invexapi, and the code that reproduces every result is available at https://github.com/samuelpinilla/waveX.

papers.title: Calculating correlation functions in integrable spin chains from local conserved charges and currents
papers.abstract: We develop a simple algebraic method for calculating correlation functions in integrable spin chains. We introduce current minors, antisymmetrized products of local conserved charge densities and their currents, and prove that their expectation values are determinants of density and current mean values. Decomposing local operators into current minors, we derive factorized formulas for correlation functions in terms of current mean values, valid in any nondegenerate eigenstate. Applying the method to the spin-$1/2$ XXZ chain and, more generally, to every representation of the Temperley--Lieb algebra, we prove previously conjectured factorized formulas for short-distance correlation functions.

papers.title: The Maxwell Bethe-Sommerfeld problem I: Thin-layer induction and results for planar TE modes
papers.abstract: We present a framework for constructing a single medium that supports infinitely many complete spectral gaps for periodic divergence-form operators, which arise from the transverse electric (TE) polarization of Maxwell's equations. The construction proceeds by inductively inserting a seed medium with a prescribed spectral gap into a thin layer of the unit cell. As a result, we obtain densely many counterexamples to the Bethe-Sommerfeld Conjecture (BSC) for divergence-form operators. Moreover, we prove that the thin-layer construction controls the gap topology: by carefully selecting the seed medium, one can realize a single operator with any prescribed configuration of gap Chern numbers. This is the first of two papers that contains all the fundamental ingredients for the thin-layer induction. In the second paper, we will apply this framework to disprove the BSC for the full three-dimensional Maxwell operator.
authors: Habib Ammari, Yu Gao, Jiayu Qiu

papers.title: Quantum-Enhanced Passive and Active Radio-Frequency Photonic Imaging
papers.abstract: Radio-frequency (RF) photonics enables broadband, phase-coherent sensing beyond the reach of purely electronic architectures, yet at a given optical carrier power its sensitivity is bounded by the standard quantum limit of the optical readout. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that this limit can be surpassed in both passive and active RF imaging modalities by encoding RF signals onto a bright phase-squeezed optical carrier and recovering them via balanced homodyne detection, while the RF front end, illumination, and image reconstruction remain classical. A unified measurement model shows that phase squeezing reduces the variance of the additive readout noise by a single factor $g$, yielding peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) gains of up to $2G$, where $G\equiv10\log_{10}(1/g)$: between $G$ and $2G$ for deterministic targets in active imaging when the classical noise of the echoes is negligible against the readout noise, and set by the ratio of scene noise to readout noise in passive imaging. We validate the model in an experiment in the 5--20 MHz band, in which synthesized RF scenes are replayed through a physical squeezed-light receiver. With 3 dB of squeezing, the PSNR improves by about 6 dB, close to $2G$, in the readout-noise-dominated regime of both modalities, and the model predicts the measured gains without free parameters. These results identify where squeezed-light readout benefits RF-photonic imaging: wherever the optical readout noise, rather than the scene or the RF front end, dominates the image error.
authors: Visuttha Manthamkarn, Haowei Shi, Shuaifeng Guo, Christopher M. Jones, Quntao Zhuang, Zheshen Zhang

papers.title: Energy-flow bubbles at the Schwarzschild horizon and their Regge-pole clock
papers.abstract: For a circularly polarized plane wave scattered by a Schwarzschild black hole, the time-averaged energy flow on the side of the horizon facing the wave contains small, sealed recirculation cells. In the main family, pairs of zero circles are born on the axis and slide into the horizon in periodic frequency windows; at higher frequencies further cells appear off the axis. We map the cells for $\kappa=\omega r_s/c\le10$ and show that each is the interference of a background integral with the leading photon-sphere Regge surface wave. A cell can die only at a zero of the circularly polarized field on the horizon, and all sixteen measured deaths are such zeros. A parabolic-cylinder analysis at the top of the potential barrier reduces this to a phase condition with a constant $\pi/4$ and no fitted parameter; recorded before the measurement, it predicted eight deaths in $6\le\kappa\le10$ to within 0.012 in $\kappa$. Electromagnetic duality makes the core of each main-family cell a circle of linear polarization; inside such a cell, flow lines lie on nested tori and close into torus knots of one chirality.

papers.title: A feedback-driven central limit theorem with $q$-Gaussian limits
papers.abstract: We establish a central limit theorem, the feedback-driven central limit theorem, for sums whose summands are independent noise variables multiplied by an amplitude that depends on the preceding normalized sum $y$. The summands are martingale differences whose conditional variance, $c+b\,y^{2}$, depends quadratically on $y$, with feedback strength $b$; unlike in the martingale central limit theorem, this conditional variance does not settle to a constant. The noise has finite variance; for positive feedback we assume, as in Lyapunov's theorem, a finite third moment, and for negative feedback bounded noise, so that the conditional variance stays nonnegative. For positive feedback, the normalized sum converges to a Student law, equivalently a $q$-Gaussian with $1<q<2$, independently of the noise distribution. For negative feedback, it converges to a compactly supported density, which is a $q$-Gaussian with $q<1$ when $-\tfrac12<b<0$. The Gaussian law, $q=1$, is recovered at zero feedback, while the Cauchy law, $q=2$, is obtained only as a limiting case, in a triangular array in which the feedback grows slowly with the number of terms. Thus every $q<2$ is obtained for a fixed feedback strength, and $q=2$ as a limit.
