We derive its Pauli-transfer representation and the corresponding quantum Fisher information (QFI) for arbitrary mixed qubit probes. We then distinguish raw QFI, which for an optimal decoded probe may remain simultaneously present in a decoded output and its complement, from decoder-accessible QFI, which is operationally single-use because a first decryption destroys the shared syndrome information needed for a second standard recovery. For $n\geq2$ encrypted clones, the effective channel family is independent of clone number up to a clone-parity-dependent permutation of the Pauli axes (the single-clone case is exceptional for $Y$-sensing, where the decoded map stays unitary). This produces a metrological parity switch: for fixed probe and generator, even and odd clone numbers can yield respectively vanishing and maximal QFI. Closed expressions are obtained for the degradation of this parity contrast under probe depolarization and Pauli-diagonal Bloch-vector contraction.

papers.title: Dynamical theory of the East model. I. A review on the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism
papers.abstract: The East model is a paradigmatic kinetically constrained spin model in one dimension that exhibits glassy dynamics. This review surveys the progress on the theoretical description of the dynamics of the East model, focusing on the spin time correlation function and the relaxation time. We summarize rigorous results on the super-Arrhenius scaling of the relaxation time in the low-temperature limit. We then present a unified derivation of the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism for both the fluctuation and domain bases. Within this formalism, an infinite hierarchy of coupled equations for the time correlation function and memory kernels emerges---a structure reminiscent of generalized mode-coupling theory developed for supercooled liquids. We review the analytical approximations obtained by truncating or closing the hierarchy at first or second orders and compare them against Monte Carlo simulations. Although these approaches perform reasonably at moderate temperatures, they universally fail in the low-temperature regime: mode-coupling closure schemes in the fluctuation basis introduce spurious ergodicity-breaking transitions, while truncations in the domain basis discard slower modes and fail to capture the asymptotic divergence of the relaxation time. The loss of analytical tractability beyond second order remains the central obstacle, underscoring the fundamental difficulty of describing hierarchical relaxation even in this ``simplest'' model of glassy dynamics.

papers.title: Static Bounds on Thermal Fast Scrambling
papers.abstract: Scrambling, the process by which initially localized quantum information spreads across an interacting many-body system, is a hallmark of quantum chaos and plays a central role in understanding black hole dynamics. In thermal systems, the chaos bound of Maldacena, Shenker and Stanford limits the exponential growth rate of out-of-time-order correlations to $2\pi/\beta$, assuming that time-ordered correlation functions factorize after a dissipation time. Establishing the corresponding rigorous logarithmic lower bounds on scrambling times at arbitrary fixed temperature has remained an open problem, most notably in disordered systems, where the Gibbs state depends on the same random couplings that drive the dynamics. Here we prove such bounds at every fixed temperature for the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model and for random $k$-local spin systems, without assuming real-time factorization. Our approach uses the operator-size distribution of the square root of the Gibbs state to quantify how local probes modify its structure. This static information bounds the thermal correlator uniformly in time along the edges of its analytic strip in complex time, and analyticity then limits how rapidly scrambling can develop. For both families of models, we prove that with probability tending to one the scrambling time is at least $(1-\epsilon)[\beta/(2\pi)]\log N$ for any $0<\epsilon<1$, with the coefficient $\beta/(2\pi)$ suggested by the chaos bound. The bound holds for each fixed pair of distinct Majorana modes in the SYK model and for the target average of any fixed single-site source in the spin model. These results place the thermal fast-scrambling timescale on a rigorous footing and show how static properties of the Gibbs state can constrain real-time information spreading.
authors: Yixuan Ma, Weikang Li, Dong-Ling Deng

papers.title: Global bound-state spectrum and spin- and angular-momentum-dependent confinement in an inverse-$3/2$ magnetic quantum dot
papers.abstract: We investigate the bound-state spectrum and confinement thresholds of a two-dimensional electron governed by the Schr\"{o}dinger--Pauli equation in an inverse-$3/2$ radial magnetic-field profile. The radial problem reduces to the biconfluent Heun equation, but instead of restricting the solution to the quasi-exact polynomial sector, we impose the bound-state condition globally through a spectral Wronskian between the endpoint-selected Frobenius solution and the subdominant asymptotic solution. The resulting spectrum contains continuous nonpolynomial bound-state branches on which the known quasi-exact solutions appear as isolated exact points. In this global description, the polynomial index $N$ remains a termination index within the quasi-exact sector but does not uniquely label the spectral branches. An independent exact analysis of the continuum edge yields spin- and angular-momentum-dependent critical couplings that can lie below the quasi-exact restriction $U_0a>4$, where $U_0$ is the Coulomb-strength parameter and $a$ is the magnetic-profile length scale. These results establish quasi-exact solvability as a set of special analytic points embedded in a broader biconfluent-Heun spectrum with spin- and angular-momentum-dependent confinement thresholds.

papers.title: Transferable neural-network preconditioners for Wilson--Clover propagator inversions
papers.abstract: We investigate two single--layer neural-network architectures for accelerating four-dimensional Wilson--Clover propagator inversions on lattice ensembles in practical use; both transfer directly without retraining. The first is a gauge-covariant parallel transport convolution (PTC) network that directly reduces the number of generalized conjugate residual (GCR) solver iterations. The second is a CNN-like network used together with a multigrid-inspired algorithm. The two approaches can be combined to further reduce GCR iterations. PTC transfers without retraining across lattice volumes, lattice spacings, and pion masses while maintaining comparable acceleration, whereas the CNN-like network transfers directly from small- to large-volume ensembles with strong acceleration. A cost comparison accounting for both basis construction and solves shows that the proposed scheme is more advantageous for large-volume ensembles than for small-volume ones.
authors: Shiyi Zhong, Yuanyi Zhang, Jian-Hui Zhang, Dian-Jun Zhao

papers.title: Two-Dimensional Kowalevski Top Problem as the Genus Two Full Jacobi Inversion Problem -Formulation Using Kolossoff Variables-
papers.abstract: For the Kowalevski top, we introduce another variable in addition to time variable, and formulate as the two-dimensional model. In this paper, since the results for the genus two full Jacobi inversion problem for the two variables Kowalevski top are already known, we utilize these results in reverse, introducing Kolossoff variables, to derive a more transparent formulation of the genus two full Jacobi inversion problem. Since there are two implicit equations of motion using Kowalevski variables, we derived two explicit equations of motion using Kolossoff variables, which is different from the Kolossoff method to derive only one explicit equation and to use Hamiltonian-Jacobi theory.

papers.title: How many events does entanglement-based positronium imaging need? Information limits of Compton polarimetry with CZT detectors
papers.abstract: The degree of polarisation correlation of the two annihilation photons, measured by Compton polarimetry, has been proposed as a PET biomarker of tissue microstructure, but the statistics it requires have not been quantified. We parameterise the measurement by the linear-polarisation correlation coefficient $\kappa$ ($\kappa=1$ maximally entangled, $1/2$ separable), derive the classical Fisher information of double-Compton events and compare it with the quantum Fisher information, relate $\kappa$ to the annihilation channels of positronium in tissue, and simulate pixelated CdZnTe (CZT) rings. The model is checked against three published measurements and an independent GATE/Geant4 simulation. A double-Compton event carries at most 0.12-0.14 units of Fisher information about $\kappa$ and 0.015 on average, 0.1-0.6% of the quantum limit. Event-wise maximum likelihood reaches the Cramer-Rao bound, whereas the conventional ratio R needs 1.2-2.3 times more events. The observed coefficient is $\kappa_{obs}=1-\alpha(1-\kappa_{pick})$, with a pick-off share $\alpha$ of 0.13-0.29 in tissue; it is sensitive to lipid fraction but not to oxygen, and carries no tissue information if pick-off photons are maximally entangled. Published porous-polymer data imply $\kappa_{pick}$ = 0.34-0.58. In a 15-mm CZT module, ordering ambiguity, position errors and electron transport roughly halve the information per event, and sequence reconstruction of multi-site events recovers this loss. With $^{18}$F and an eight-module ring, $\kappa$ can be measured to $\pm0.01$ in a 10-mm tumour, but separating tissues by $\kappa$ alone requires 6-74 times more decays than are available.
authors: Haitao Zhou, Ruonan Wang, Jianyong Hu, Zhifang Wu, Sijin Li

papers.title: Maximum entropy reconstruction of the black hole greybody factors from its Korteweg-de Vries integrals
papers.abstract: The dynamics of perturbed non-rotating black holes (BHs) can be described by master wave equations with a potential barrier. Recent work has shown that these equations possess an infinite number of symmetries generated by the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) hierarchy, leading to conserved quantities (KdV integrals) that fully determine the BH greybody factors via a moment problem. In this paper, we introduce and validate a new method to solve this moment problem using the maximum entropy principle. The method reconstructs, at each order of truncation, the least-biased transmission probability compatible with a finite set of KdV integrals, guaranteeing positivity by construction. We first validate the technique against the exactly solvable P\"oschl-Teller potential. We then apply it to the Regge-Wheeler potential governing axial perturbations of a Schwarzschild BH, where no exact solution is available; the resulting reconstruction agrees closely with the fourth-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation across several multipoles. This is the first application of the maximum entropy method to the reconstruction of BH greybody factors, demonstrating that a modest number of KdV integrals is sufficient to recover them accurately.
authors: Noah Alberca (Departament de Matem\`atiques, Universitat Aut\`onoma de Barcelona, Institute of Space Sciences), Michele Lenzi (Physique Th\'eorique et Math\'ematique, Universit\'e Libre de Bruxelles), Carlos F. Sopuerta (Institute of Space Sciences, Institute of Space Studies of Catalonia)

papers.title: Relaxing the i.i.d. state preparation assumption with the block QKD protocol
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a novel approach to handling the independent and identically distributed assumption for the state preparation in prepare-and measure QKD protocols. Contrary to previous approaches, we do not prove the security using sub-protocols, and instead opt to guarantee security in the presence of correlations by dividing the communication into finite blocks of consecutive pulses, and adding an additional assumption of no dependence between each block. In turn we obtain a protocol which uses only a relaxed i.i.d. assumption and is easier to implement than subprotocol-style approaches since it does not require separate statistics for each sub-protocol, whose number grows with the correlation length of the underlying dependency.

papers.title: The $N$-channel white-noise Schr\"odinger operator in all three Dyson classes. I. Explicit stationary admittance distribution, density of states and outgoing Kontsevich matrix Airy integrals
papers.abstract: We obtain an explicit stationary distribution of the matrix Riccati variable---the boundary admittance---for an $N$-channel Schr\"odinger operator with Gaussian white-noise disorder, in all three Dyson symmetry classes $\beta=1,2,4$. Uniform absorption regularizes the Riccati dynamics, and the distribution's normalization factorizes into outgoing Kontsevich matrix Airy integrals. This gives a common route to the density of states and the sum of Lyapunov exponents, extending Halperin's scalar solution to coupled channels. Exact finite-$N$ formulas connect two spectral regimes: the Lifshitz tail, including its symmetry-dependent prefactor, and the collective large-$N$ edge. We reduce the $\beta=4$ and even-$N$ $\beta=1$ problems to unitary orthogonal polynomials and an auxiliary recursion. Their critical double-scaling limit yields edge profiles on the $N^{-4/5}$ energy scale, governed by a complex Painlev\'e-I tritronqu\'ee solution and a linear auxiliary equation. We conjecture that these profiles describe a universal edge regime of random band matrices.

papers.title: Success Probability of Block-Encoding Methods
papers.abstract: Block-encoding methods apply nonunitary functions $f(\widetilde H)$ of a normalized Hermitian operator on a quantum computer, but only upon a successful postselection, which introduces a shot overhead rarely included in resource estimates. We analyze the success probability $p^{(f)}_{\mathrm{success}}=\sum_n w_n|f(\tilde E_n)|^2$ of three constructions, namely linear combination of unitaries (LCU), qubitization and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT), where $w_n$ are the weights of the input state on the eigenstates of $\widetilde H$. Using the one-dimensional Hubbard model with up to 14 sites (35 qubits), we show that for LCU, the success probability is bounded by the squared ratio between the spectral norm and the $1$-norm of the Pauli decomposition, and that for a Hartree--Fock input it plateaus with system size while the ground-state overlap keeps decreasing. For qubitization, it oscillates with the Chebyshev degree, and favorable degrees can be identified from a few dominant spectral components or predicted from shallow-degree data. For QSVT, the polynomial normalization constant directly sets the success probability, and a tight certified bound balances it against phase-finding robustness. An application to quantum Krylov methods shows a nonuniform shot overhead across Krylov moments. The success probability should therefore be part of the resource estimation of block-encoding-based algorithms.
authors: Oumaya Ladhari, Matthieu Sauban\`ere, J\'er\'emie Messud

papers.title: Subwavelength confinement of optical and acoustic waves for enhancing Brillouin gain in a planar waveguide structure
papers.abstract: We propose a planar waveguide structure consisting of two layers separated by a gap that provides subwavelength confinement of optical and acoustic modes and a large overlap integral between them. This, in turn, leads to an increase in Brillouin gain. Using the structure of two Si$_3$N$_4$ layers with a subwavelength gap from SiO$_2$ as an example, we demonstrate that a hybridized transverse-magnetic (TM) optical mode exhibits strong field confinement in the SiO$_2$ gap. Simultaneously, a high-frequency acoustic mode can be confined in the same gap, providing a high spatial overlap between the optical and acoustic fields. This provides a high opto-acoustic interaction with a Brillouin gain up to $5$ W$^{-1}$m$^{-1}$. The proposed structure is compatible with planar photonic integration and offers a promising platform for compact, low-threshold Brillouin lasers and coherent phonon generation.
authors: A. R. Mukhamedyanov, E. A. Tereshchenkov, E. S. Andrianov, A. A. Zyablovsky

papers.title: Closing the loop on memory: accurate, shallow and transferable decoding of quantum LDPC codes
papers.abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes have attracted interest for fault-tolerant quantum computing because their high-rate constructions offer a route to reduced qubit overhead. Realizing this potential requires reliable decoding. Belief propagation (BP) forms the basis of many qLDPC decoders, but can fail to converge under circuit-level noise. Memory-based variants can improve convergence, yet selecting memory strengths that work reliably across different syndromes remains challenging. Here we introduce TEMPO-BP, which adapts each variable's memory strength to the evolving decoding state through local feedback. On the gross code at a physical error rate of 0.4%, single-run TEMPO-BP achieves a per-shot logical failure rate of 0.73%, compared with 2.51% for BP+OSD+CS-10. Ensembles of 10-15 concurrent instances match or lower failure counts relative to Relay-BP-5 at all ten tested operating points, with per-instance iteration caps at least tenfold lower than its serial limit. Without retuning, the gross-code parameters yield fewer observed failures than Relay-BP-5 in its published gross-code configuration across four additional code families. Ablations support state-dependent memory control, while a loop-gain analysis characterizes specific amplification modes in the decoding dynamics.
authors: Zhou You, Ying Li, Xiao Yuan, Yuan Yao

papers.title: A hyperhamiltonian approach to symmetry of the Dirac equation
papers.abstract: The Dirac equation is the simplest wave equation invariant under the Poincar\'e group, and was indeed determined by Dirac precisely by requiring this invariance. Moreover it is invariant under dilations of the wave function, as follows by its linear character. It is known that the Dirac equation possesses, besides these, other symmetries, which in this sense are the special part of the Dirac equation's full symmetry. In previous work we have shown that the Dirac equation can be cast in hyperhamiltonian terms. Here we show that the symmetries can also be described in hyperhamiltonian terms.

papers.title: Higher-point amplitudes and recursion relations from the worldsheet in complex Liouville string
papers.abstract: We consider multipoint perturbative string amplitudes in genus zero in complex Liouville string theory (CLS) in the worldsheet approach. Based on explicit worldsheet calculations and analytic bootstrap, we first compute correlators involving ground ring operators, which additionally depend on a choice of integration cycle on the moduli space. Using this result and higher equations of motion in Liouville theory, we calculate higher-point tachyon correlators with one degenerate field and explain what contributions were missed in previous attempts to apply this method in the literature. This allows us to derive a recursion formula, which agrees with the general recursion for amplitudes known from "matrix model" approach to CLS. We also propose an expression for correlators with ground ring insertions in terms of tautological classes on the moduli space of curves and comment on generalization of these results to the case of rational minimal strings.

papers.title: Reversal of dynamical backaction and cooling below the quantum backaction limit in Floquet-driven multimode optomechanical resonators
papers.abstract: Dynamical backaction describes how a driven cavity field responds with delay to mechanical motion, and can be used to cool that motion toward its quantum ground state or amplify it into self-oscillation. Control over this interaction underpins laser cooling, high-fidelity state preparation, quantum transduction, and phonon lasing. In conventional cavity optomechanics, both the sign and the magnitude of the optical damping are dictated by the laser detuning, and cooling is bounded by quantum backaction (QBA), the optomechanical analogue of the Doppler limit in cold atoms. We show, in theory and experiment, that dynamical backaction can be strongly enhanced in multimode optomechanical resonators driven by time-varying (Floquet) optical fields. A modulated drive couples a sideband-unresolved MHz mode to a sideband-resolved GHz mode through the shared cavity, replacing the QBA limit of the target mode by the occupancy of the auxiliary mode. Experimentally, we cool the MHz mode to $47 \pm 13$ phonons, about half its single-mode QBA limit and an order of magnitude below what single-tone backaction reaches at the same intracavity photon number. The character of the interaction can moreover be completely inverted at fixed laser detuning, turning cooling into amplification and vice versa, controlled solely by the modulation frequency. Floquet driving thus extends open-loop quantum control, which requires no measurement or feedback, to mechanical resonators outside the resolved-sideband regime.
authors: Menno H. Jansen, Roel Burgwal, Ewold Verhagen

papers.title: Global analysis of the $\rho$ resonance in lattice QCD
papers.abstract: We present a lattice-QCD study of the $\rho$ resonance in which we address the quark-mass and lattice-spacing dependence in a novel way using a global analysis of four $N_f=2+1$ ensembles. We parametrize discretization effects in the lattice energy levels and not in the scattering amplitude, which is defined in the continuum. We describe the amplitude using a $K$-matrix parameterization, which contains the light- and strange-quark mass dependence. By varying the parameterizations of quark-mass and lattice-spacing dependence, we examine the sensitivity of the physical-limit $\rho$ pole position to these choices and obtain the result $\sqrt{s}_\rho = 744(11)(7) - i\,69(7)(3)~\text{MeV}$ from a model average.
authors: Luka Jevsenak, Luka Leskovec, Stefan Meinel, John Negele, Srijit Paul, Andrew Pochinsky

papers.title: Stabilizer-Restricted Antidistinguishability in Quantum Computation with Magic States
papers.abstract: An antidistinguishing measurement for a family of preparations excludes at least one preparation for every possible outcome, constraining 'classical' representations of these processes, known as ontological models. We develop this connection within quantum computing with magic states (QCM), a universal model of quantum computation. Our constructions use adaptive Pauli measurements on tensor products of single-qubit non stabilizer states, including families associated with the Clifford hierarchy. These constructions yield stabilizer-restricted versions of the Pusey-Barrett-Rudolph theorem: any ontological model reproducing these measurement statistics and satisfying preparation independence must assign disjoint ontic supports to the preparations considered. We demonstrate this obstruction to preparation independence in a concrete ontological model based on convex polytopes used for the classical simulation of QCM.

papers.title: Group classification and equivalence of two classes of evolution equations of arbitrary order
papers.abstract: We revisit the group classification of the $(1{+}1)$-dimensional evolution equations $u_t=F(u_n)$ and $u_t+uu_x=F(u_n)$ of arbitrary order $n\geq2$, where $u_n=\partial_x^n u$, and describe the usual point equivalence groups of the two classes. We recover the known contact equivalences between the three second-order equations with seven-dimensional maximal Lie invariance algebras and extend the hodograph construction to points where $u_x=0$. For $n>2$, the dimensions of the contact symmetry algebras distinguish the two classes. We give reciprocal transformations linking the two classes at order three and formulate a nonlocal classification problem. We also classify the extensions of the Lie invariance algebra of the Burgers equation in a wider class of Galilei-invariant equations.
authors: Vyacheslav M. Boyko, Oleksandra V. Lokaziuk

papers.title: Thermal deep inelastic scattering, universality and complex geodesics
papers.abstract: In deep inelastic scattering (DIS), a lepton scatters off a target hadron whose structure is probed by an exchanged photon with large spacelike virtuality. We consider two-point functions of currents in strongly interacting quantum field theories at finite temperature in this kinematic regime and use a holographic description to compute them. At large virtuality, the crossover from vacuum-dominated to thermally dominated physics corresponds to a transition from exponentially suppressed absorption to power-law behavior of the response functions. This regime is related to a particular near-lightcone limit of thermal CFT correlators. We show that the response functions exhibit a large degree of universality: the dependence on the three-point couplings of currents to the stress tensor enters through a channel-dependent coefficient multiplying the kinematic parameter that controls the relative size of vacuum and thermal effects. The same coefficient controls conformal collider bounds; when either bound is saturated, the corresponding response function takes its vacuum form in the near-lightcone limit. Furthermore, the absorption exponent in the low-temperature regime is related to a complex geodesic propagating in the near-lightcone geometry.

papers.title: Entropy of Noncommutative Spaces
papers.abstract: We give an overview of the second quantisation of spectral triples and compute the entropy of the noncommutative space described by it in terms of a spectral action. This reviews earlier work by Chamseddine, Connes and the second author, but presented here concisely, including the procedure of second quantisation using infinite-dimensional Clifford algebras. We exemplify the theory by considering noncommutative metric spaces consisting of $N$ points. The entropy of these discrete spaces is explicitly computed, and we study the resulting entropic force as well as the evolution of the spaces in time.
authors: Cisca Kalmijn, Walter D. van Suijlekom

papers.title: Deterministic nonlinear domain engineering algorithm with variable sub-coherence-length domains
papers.abstract: We present a new and improved deterministic algorithm that calculates the poling domains for the implementation of arbitrary phase-matching functions (PMF) in quasi-phase-matched nonlinear crystals for parametric down-conversion photon sources. In contrast to previous work, the algorithm presented here makes full use of the limits of the fabrication process, such as the minimum feature size and resolution of the lithographic process underpinning the poling procedure. This minimizes the tracking error to the target electric field and improves the accuracy in reaching the desired PMF. We give a tutorial on how to calculate the target function for arbitrary PMFs and run the algorithm. We also demonstrate the procedure on a relevant application in quantum sensing, where we use a quadratic phase on the PMF to implement a broadband photon spectrum while maintaining high nonlinearity across the crystal. The designed crystal is experimentally tested, and the result matches expectations.
authors: Michael Schlosser, Tommaso Faleo, Gregor Weihs, Robert Keil, Stefan Frick

papers.title: Observation of Crossover from Repulsive to Attractive Interactions between Two $nS$-Rydberg Atoms in Dual-Species Atom Arrays
papers.abstract: Dual-species Rydberg atom arrays provide a flexible platform for engineering long-range interactions beyond the conventional isotropic blockade regime. We spectroscopically study interactions between different $s$-state Rydberg levels in a $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$--$^{85}\mathrm{Rb}$ optical-tweezer array. By varying the principal-quantum-number difference $\Delta n$ around $61S_{1/2}$, we observe a crossover from repulsive to attractive interactions. We identify a distinct regime at $\Delta n=2$ in which F\"orster-enhanced electronic spin exchange dominates over orbital exchange and produces a strongly bond-orientation-dependent pair spectrum. Time-domain collective-excitation measurements reveal this geometry-dependent spin exchange through a pronounced anisotropy of the double-excitation probability. For $\Delta n=1$, by contrast, orbital exchange dominates and the interaction is nearly isotropic. These results establish the principal-quantum-number difference and bond orientation as complementary control parameters for tailoring Rydberg interaction spectra and collective excitation dynamics, opening new opportunities for engineering spin-dependent Hamiltonians in programmable atom arrays.
authors: Yi Chen, Kun-Peng Wang, Ming-Rui Wei, Peng Zhang, Yang Wang, Yi-Bo Wang, Min Liu, Peng Xu, Xue-Yuan Wang, Xiang Gao, Chengshu Li, Xiao-Dong He, Ming-Sheng Zhan

papers.title: Precise Analytic Boundaries and Positive Symplectic Paths in the Stability Diagrams of Elliptic Relative Equilibria
papers.abstract: We investigate the dependence of the linear stability of elliptic relative equilibria on the mass parameter and eccentricity. Using a periodic matrix Riccati decomposition, we derive explicit analytic curves separating hyperbolic--hyperbolic and complex--saddle spectra. The construction applies to the Lagrangian, Euler--Robe, and $(2+2)$-body families. A Hermitian Riccati factorization also yields an eccentricity-independent sufficient condition for positivity of the associated operators under every unit-circle boundary condition, and hence for hyperbolicity of the monodromy matrix. Finally, we construct an explicit lower bound for the second antiperiodic degeneracy curve by a finite trigonometric test function. This bound agrees with the value and tangent of the degeneracy curve at the circular limit. Together, these results provide analytic descriptions and estimates for distinct spectral boundaries in the stability diagrams.

papers.title: Coalescing and annihilating random walks on the ring
papers.abstract: We study correlation functions in the model of coalescing and annihilating random walks on the one-dimensional periodic lattice $\mathbb{Z}_N$. We prove that, for a special class of initial conditions, the $n$-point correlation function can be represented as a linear combination of two Pfaffians of $2n\times 2n$ matrices constructed from $2\times2$ matrix kernels, which in turn can be expressed in terms of two scalar kernels. This is an analogue of the single-Pfaffian form exhibited by correlation functions of the same model on $\mathbb{Z}$, where it serves as a signature of a Pfaffian point process. We derive equations for the kernels and construct their solutions. We also show that a particular example of an initial condition leading to bi-Pfaffian correlation functions is the inhomogeneous Bernoulli point process, which includes a fixed initial configuration as a particular limiting case.
authors: A. M. Povolotsky, R. Tribe, O. V. Zaboronski

papers.title: No complete set of mutually unbiased bases in dimension ten contains the Fourier pair or three product bases
papers.abstract: With computer-assisted proofs that $\mathbb{C}^6$ admits at most three mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) now available, $\mathbb{C}^{10}$ is the smallest dimension in which it is unknown whether a complete set of $d+1=11$ MUBs exists; only three MUBs are known. We prove that every triple of mutually unbiased product bases of $\mathbb{C}^2\otimes\mathbb{C}^5$ is strongly unextendible: no vector is unbiased to all three bases. Consequently no set of four MUBs in dimension ten, and in particular no complete set, contains three product bases. This settles the case $d=2\times5$ anticipated by McNulty, Pammer and Weigert; it was known only for the Heisenberg-Weyl triple. The proof covers all ten equivalence classes with explicit Nullstellensatz certificates modulo one prime on $91$ charts of $\mathbb{P}^9\times\mathbb{P}^9$ for each class ($910$ in all), transferred to characteristic zero by a projective reduction lemma, together with an independent rank certificate for eight of the ten classes. We also prove that the pair formed by the standard and the Fourier basis of $\mathbb{C}^{10}$ is contained in no set of four MUBs. Exactly $3040$ rays are unbiased to both bases (this confirms the count found numerically by F\"uhr and Rzeszotnik), each of them is unbiased to at most eight of the others, and every triple formed by the pair and a third MUB is strongly unextendible. For this we certify $34,940$ cyclic $10$-roots in Krawczyk uniqueness boxes, decide unimodularity exactly through an involution, and prove completeness by a four-dimensional interval branch-and-bound obtained from the Chinese-remainder splitting $\mathbb{Z}_{10}=\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_5$.
authors: Jinze Yang, Yile Liu, Yangyang Li, Xiu-Hao Deng

papers.title: Separations Between Randomized and Exact Quantum Query Complexity for Boolean Functions
papers.abstract: We construct a family of total Boolean functions $F_{\mathrm{tot}}$ whose randomized and exact quantum query complexities satisfy $R(F_{\mathrm{tot}}) \ge Q_E(F_{\mathrm{tot}})^{2-o(1)}$. Chiruvella, Kayal, Mittal, Paraashar, and Saurabh (2026) also obtained a nearly quadratic separation for total functions in the query model by a different method. For every fixed $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, we construct a family of partial Boolean functions $F_{\mathrm{par}}$ on $n$ bits satisfying $Q_E(F_{\mathrm{par}})=O_\varepsilon(1)$ and $R(F_{\mathrm{par}})=\Omega_\varepsilon(n^{1-\varepsilon})$. This matches the asymptotic separation previously obtained with bounded error (STOC 2021; SICOMP 2023). Lifting yields a family of partial communication functions $G_{\mathrm{par}}$ with $Q_E^{\mathrm{cc}}(G_{\mathrm{par}})=O_\varepsilon(\log n)$ and $R^{\mathrm{pub,cc}}(G_{\mathrm{par}})=\Omega_\varepsilon(n^{1-\varepsilon})$, where $n$ is the total number of input bits held by the two parties.

papers.title: Interaction Landscapes of Structurally Distorted Toroidal Classical Spin Textures
papers.abstract: We develop a classical discrete magnetostatic model of localized magnetic moments arranged in a toroidal texture, where the moments are represented by static current loops and study the behavior of the magnetic dipole-dipole interaction under several types of structural deformations. The purpose is to disentangle effects due to geometric and magnetic deformations, including elliptical, lopsided, alternating, and tilted configurations. In particular, we investigate how distortions modify the toroidal moment and the interaction energy between pairs of toroidal structures. The resulting interaction landscapes exhibit characteristic symmetry patterns and anisotropies that are highly sensitive to the underlying deformation. As a separate proof-of-concept comparison, first-principles calculations on a molecular spin-toroidal system reveal qualitatively similar orientation-dependent behavior. The calculated interaction is microscopically the conventional pairwise magnetic dipole-dipole interaction between localized moments arranged in a spin-toroidal texture; the toroidal moment characterizes the collective texture and should not be interpreted as introducing an additional elementary interaction term. Our results provide a platform for exploring orientation-dependent interactions of spin-toroidal textures in molecular magnets and related nanoscale magnetic systems that are essential to understand the role of toroidal order.
authors: Henry Pommer, Arkamita Bandyopadhyay, Jamal Berakdar

papers.title: Torsional Hall Viscosity of Massive Chern Insulators: Finite Temperature and Chemical Potential
papers.abstract: We study the torsional Hall viscosity $\zeta_{\rm H}$ of Chern insulators at finite temperature and chemical potential. Our analysis considers the massive Dirac fermion and two deformations: a constant out-of-plane magnetic field and a momentum-dependent mass described by the single-block Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (BHZ) Hamiltonian. For the massive Dirac theory, we show that temperature and chemical potential lead to UV-finite corrections and that a chemical potential outside the bulk gap modifies $\zeta_{\rm H}$ even at zero temperature. In a constant magnetic field, the response of massive Dirac fermions is dictated by the relativistic Landau-level spectrum, leading to a plateau structure at zero temperature that is smoothed at finite temperature. The jumps are proportional to the Dirac mass and inversely proportional to the squared magnetic length and the newly occupied Landau-level energy. Finally, we present a detailed study of the correction to $\zeta_{\rm H}$ in the single-block BHZ continuum model due to temperature and chemical potential. For parameters relevant to (Hg,Mn)Te quantum wells, the magnitude of the jump across a mass domain wall retains its vacuum enhancement due to the BHZ deformation as long as the chemical potential lies sufficiently deep inside the gap compared with the thermal energy. Our results extend the theory of torsional Hall viscosity to experimentally relevant conditions and may facilitate its future detection.
authors: Weizhen Jia, Ioannis Matthaiakakis, David Rodr\'iguez Fern\'andez, Zhuo-Yu Xian, Johanna Erdmenger, Ewelina M. Hankiewicz, Ren\'e Meyer

papers.title: Weak lensing data beyond flexion
papers.abstract: In weak lensing, shear and convergence are well studied and have provided a wealth of information about the distribution of matter in the universe. More recently, flexion -- the next term in the multipole expansion of the lensing potential, responsible for the characteristic banana-shaped distortion of lensed images -- has been shown to provide additional constraints on the mass distribution of lensing systems, particularly for galaxy clusters. Here we investigate whether weak-lensing information beyond flexion is similarly useful for lens-mass reconstruction. Using the roulette-amplitude formalism, we construct synthetic datasets for a single SIE lens and for SIE and SIS cluster lenses, with and without simulated Gaussian noise, and perform a least-squares reconstruction of the lens parameters using amplitudes truncated at third (flexion), fourth, and fifth order. As a proof of concept, we find that higher-order amplitudes do provide additional, useful information: the benefit is modest for a single lens, where flexion already constrains most parameters, but becomes substantial for cluster lenses, where the rotation and ellipticity are otherwise poorly recovered. The improvement is most pronounced in the presence of noise, where third-order reconstruction can become unreliable while higher-order amplitudes restore much of the lost accuracy. These results suggest that, as weak-lensing surveys grow in depth and precision, data beyond flexion could meaningfully improve mass reconstruction for the most complex and noisiest lensing systems, motivating further work using observational rather than synthetic data.
authors: Ben D. Normann, Martin H. Enoksen, Nicol\`o Oreste Pinciroli Vago, Hans Georg Schaathun

papers.title: Specifying & Verifying Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
papers.abstract: Building quantum computers is challenging due to the noise that affects qubits. Quantum error correction tackles noise by encoding information in quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes. These codes are often complex, increasingly found by computational search, presented in diverse formalisms with informal arguments, and hard to reason about algorithmically. Given that the rest of the quantum computing stack relies on a QEC code's properties for correct computation, we propose a formally verified foundation for QEC codes. We present QECLean, a Lean-based framework for formally specifying and verifying QEC codes. QECLean backs every claimed QEC-code property with a machine-checked proof, unifies the diverse presentations of codes in the literature through common abstractions, and makes new codes easy to specify. We present a new compositional technique, code combinators, for proving code distance analytically. Code combinators allow us to prove the distance of large codes that are out of reach for algorithmic techniques; for example, we show that IBM's $[[360, 12, \leq 24]]$ code has distance 24, which was previously only known as an upper bound. Furthermore, we show how our approach allows us to formalize and prove entire code families, such as the surface code. Our work lays the foundation required for reasoning about circuit-level implementations of codes on given architectures and for building end-to-end verified compilers for quantum computers. QECLean is available at https://github.com/Stavan-Jain/QECLean
authors: Stavan Jain, Nithin Raveendran, Aws Albarghouthi

papers.title: What kind of quantum advantage is this?
papers.abstract: Quantum advantage encompasses fundamentally different claims, from resource reductions to exponential separations in sample complexity. Evaluating these claims requires distinguishing how an algorithm achieves an advantage from what is necessary for the separation and how strongly it is supported against classical alternatives. We propose a multi-label taxonomy that makes these distinctions explicit, classifying structural, interference, and coherent mechanisms while separately recording their necessity and the evidence for the classical comparison. Coherent mechanisms are further divided into memory and output, reflecting distinct restrictions on quantum information processing. A two-part entanglement-breaking test distinguishes loss of information from loss of algorithmic efficiency. The hidden subgroup problem illustrates the distinction: among the cases examined, cross-copy coherence is information-theoretically necessary only for the symmetric group. We present this as a diagnostic methodology rather than a theory of quantum advantage: for a new claim, it identifies the relevant adversary, separates the mechanisms a protocol uses from those shown to be necessary, and records the strength of the evidence and the quality of the advantage separately.

papers.title: A boson representation of the electronic structure calculation based on the quantum Krylov subspace algorithm
papers.abstract: Quantum calculations are expected to broaden the range of strongly correlated phenomena in solids accessible to first-principles calculations. The quantum Krylov diagonalization method, or in a broader sense, the quantum subspace expansion method (QSE) offers an advantage over other variational methods in terms of numerical stability. In this work, we propose a boson representation of electronic systems with the aim of reducing QSE quantum circuit depth, where electron-hole pair bosons serve as the fundamental degrees of freedom. We benchmark the boson representation in comparison with a corresponding fermionic QSE and CCSD for an equidistant and a dimerized configuration of a periodic hydrogen chain \ce{(H2)_n}. Despite the drastic approximation we reveal the boson QSE scheme provides practically useful accuracy in the ground state energy. Our results support its applicability to realistic quasi-two- and three-dimensional electronic systems.

papers.title: Quantum-Assisted D-FACTS Scheduling for Moving Target Defense under Switching Limits
papers.abstract: Moving target defense with distributed flexible alternating-current transmission system (D-FACTS) devices re- quires activation decisions as operating points change. Switching limits couple these decisions, but period-by-period rankings can overlook combinations needed to complete low-activation schedules. This paper proposes cross-period candidate sharing and schedule-completion evaluation to allocate limited physical checks in quantum-assisted D-FACTS scheduling. The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) generates activation candidates, while classical scheduling enforces operating and switching constraints. We also quantify model-based activation requirements and test detection through noisy nonlinear trials. A modified IEEE 118-bus study assesses recovery of reference activation and switching objectives within the evaluated set. Combining candidate sharing and schedule-completion evaluation improves final-budget recovery over period-by-period ranking in the primary operating window for every tested candidate generator. The results show that quantum and classical candidates yield identical recovery curves under combined checking, so the same allocation policy applies to either source.
authors: Hongyu Wu, Yichen Liu, Bo Liu

papers.title: SCOPE: A Physical Execution Latency-Guided Quantum Circuit Compilation Framework
papers.abstract: Quantum computing requires compilers to translate algorithms represented in the quantum circuit model into unitary operations supported by physical devices. Limited coherence time makes physical execution latency an important compilation objective. Gate fusion can shorten pulses, but gate count and depth do not capture fused targets' control demands. Evaluating every candidate with quantum optimal control (QOC) would embed pulse optimization in structural search. We present Schmidt-guided Compilation for Optimized Pulse Execution (SCOPE), driven by an operator Schmidt time surrogate. The target's angular distance from product operators measures the required nonlocal change; dividing it by a coupling-limited evolution-rate bound gives a lower bound on exact implementation time. Trace-angle and waveform constraints complete block scores for critical-path evaluation during genetic search. Local QOC determines final pulse durations. Under a numerical nearest-neighbor control model, all 104 results across 13 instances from four application families have shorter QOC critical-path durations than an adapted efficient pulse generation framework with advanced synthesis for quantum circuits (EPOC). Using eight-run instance means, the equally weighted reduction is 42.50\%, with a geometric mean speedup of 2.00. In a shared six-qubit quantum Fourier transform (QFT) ablation, time-surrogate guidance reduces mean QOC duration by 22.21\% relative to gate-count guidance and 21.01\% relative to depth guidance, validating the surrogate's joint use in fitness evaluation and mutation-region selection.
authors: Bolin Zhang, Zhiyuan Zhang, Yongguang Lv, Ruiqing He, Hengliang Guo, Jiandong Shang, Qiang Chen

papers.title: Soft momentum expansion about the Stokes topological limit of Bogoliubov coefficients
papers.abstract: It is known that particle production in time-dependent cosmological backgrounds can be computed using the Stokes phenomena occurring in Bogoliubov transformations with an analytically continued time coordinate. We analytically compute the soft momentum expansion of the particle production amplitude about the Stokes topological limit that was recently discovered in this context. The computational technique relies on an exponentially improved asymptotic expansion that involves automorphisms in the space of functions defined partly by the angular step function intrinsic to the Stokes topological sectors. We combine this with special discrete symmetries tied to the time dependence of the dispersion relation $\omega_k^2(z) = C(k) + A z^n$ for even $n$ to explicitly compute the leading momentum dependence of the amplitude which is nonperturbative in $A$. We also use this result to give a semi-analytic estimate of the number density of particles in this class of scenarios.
authors: Daniel J. H. Chung, Nidhi Sudhir, Junqi Zhang

papers.title: Deep Learning for Physicists: From Linear Regression to Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: These lecture notes are based on an introductory course on neural networks and deep learning that the author taught in the School of Mathematical Sciences at Queen Mary University of London in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The author, however, is a physicist, and it shows: wherever possible, ideas are explained with physical intuition rather than heavy formalism. Readers with a background in physics or mathematics who want a self-contained, introductory route into modern machine learning may therefore find these notes particularly friendly. The notes start from maximum likelihood, least squares, linear regression and (stochastic) gradient descent. They then cover neural networks, backpropagation, the vanishing gradient problem, batch and layer normalization, overfitting and regularization, adversarial examples, and the kernel method. The second half turns to natural language processing: word embeddings, recurrent networks and LSTMs, the attention mechanism and Transformers, and large language models, including scaling laws, the history of GPT, instruction tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, hallucination, alignment faking, chain-of-thought reasoning and test-time scaling. The emphasis on large language models reflects requests from the students. The notes are aimed at third- and fourth-year students in the UK system. Because the course was also taken by students from other departments, very little is assumed: even basic material such as matrix multiplication is explained from scratch, so readers familiar with it can safely skip such parts. No originality is claimed; the aim is a coherent, intuitive path through the material. Developments after spring 2025 are not covered, but the basic ideas emphasized here are unlikely to go out of date soon.

papers.title: Lifting asymptotic symmetries from metric to tetrad formulation
papers.abstract: Metric solution spaces defined by gauge and boundary conditions are associated with a residual symmetry algebra, consisting of the diffeomorphism generators whose action preserves these conditions. Describing a metric solution space in terms of tetrad variables adds a local Lorentz freedom. When part of this freedom is fixed by additional tetrad gauge and boundary conditions, metric residual symmetries must be supplemented by compensating Lorentz transformations. If a residual Lorentz freedom remains, there is an ambiguity in these compensating transformations. The most direct choices generally fail to realize the metric residual symmetry algebra as a subalgebra of the tetrad one, because of a field-dependent cocycle. We show that a reference tetrad, that is a section of the tetrad solution space seen as a principal bundle over the metric one, always provides a lift free of this cocycle, so that the tetrad residual symmetry algebra is the semi-direct sum of the metric one and the ideal of field-dependent residual Lorentz transformations. The construction is independent of the gauge conditions, of the residual group, of the first-order Lagrangian, and reduces to the Kosmann lift on metric isometry generators. We illustrate it on a Weyl BMS-type solution space with time-dependent boundary metric, described in tetrad variables with a residual U(1) Lorentz freedom, for which the cocycle of a naive lift is computed and then explicitly removed.

papers.title: TCBP-JOBS: GPU-Accelerated Quantum Error Correction Decoding and Noise Learning with Near-Optimal Accuracy
papers.abstract: Achieving near-optimal quantum error correction (QEC) decoding accuracy often requires computationally expensive searches that limit both large-scale simulation and real-time operation. We introduce trajectory-calibrated belief propagation (TCBP), which learns calibrated fault probabilities from BP trajectories, and jittered OSD beam search (JOBS), which uses these probabilities to guide parallel GPU searches. Across surface, color and bivariate-bicycle code memory and surgery circuits, TCBP-JOBS achieves logical error rates comparable to those of the Tesseract most-likely-error decoder at physical error rates of 0.1% to 0.4%, and up to 4.5$\times$ lower on the largest codes. Serial speedups over Tesseract's sparsified presets range from 10$\times$ to 7,400$\times$, and against unsparsified long-beam Tesseract they reach 13,000$\times$ on the bivariate-bicycle codes, at logical error rate ratios of 0.97 to 1.57. At lower physical error rates ($10^{-4}$ to $5\times10^{-4}$), rare-event splitting on the gross code shows that Tesseract is more accurate. Batched execution accelerates offline simulation for rapid, efficient exploration of large-scale QEC design spaces. For QPUs with longer logical clock cycles, our serial memory and logical-surgery experiments demonstrate accuracy comparable to Tesseract while meeting the millisecond-scale latency requirements of online feed-forward operation. Beyond memory and logic decoding, we demonstrate using TCBP-JOBS for confidence scores for postselection in memory and magic-state cultivation, enabling end-to-end color code cultivation. Together, these methods provide a GPU framework for accelerating QEC research via accurate decoding, noise estimation, and confidence assessment.
authors: Ben Howe, Satvik Maurya, Jan Olle, Ivan Basov, Muyuan Li, Justin G. Lietz, Kevin Young, Krysta M. Svore

papers.title: Detectability of Eccentric Intermediate Mass-Ratio Inspiral in the Decihertz Band
papers.abstract: The proposed decihertz gravitational-wave (GW) band $(\sim 10^{-2}-1\,\Hz)$ will observe the late inspiral of intermediate mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs), binaries with mass ratios $10^2 \lesssim q \lesssim 10^4$ that assemble dynamically in dense stellar environments and are expected to retain measurable eccentricity. Search and parameter-estimation pipelines are predominantly built around circular templates, and we test this assumption. Using black-hole perturbation theory waveforms from \textsc{FastEMRIWaveforms} for a representative IMRI ($M=10^4\,\modot$, $q=100$, observed for its final $10\,\hr$), we compute fitting factors between eccentric signals and circular templates, maximizing over the template's total mass and mass ratio with a differential-evolution search, for the B-DECIGO, LGWA-Si, and IndIGO-D noise curves and a flat PSD. The mismatch grows with initial eccentricity $e_0$ and crosses the standard $3\%$ threshold at $e_0\simeq3\times10^{-2}$, well within the range allowed by the waveform model and expected from dynamical formation. The best-fitting circular templates also bias the total mass and mass ratio by several percent at $e_0=0.1$. Combining the mismatch with the signal-to-noise-dependent distinguishability criterion, we find that for a source at $1\,\mathrm{Gpc}$, eccentricities as small as $e_0\simeq5\times10^{-4}$ (B-DECIGO and IndIGO-D) and $5\times10^{-3}$ (LGWA-Si) are resolvable, one to two orders of magnitude below where detection efficiency degrades. The loss of match arises from the excitation of radial Teukolsky harmonics, which spread power into sidebands that circular templates cannot represent, and from the slower orbital decay of eccentric binaries at fixed initial semi-latus rectum. Robust detection and parameter estimation of IMRIs with DECIGO, LGWA, and IndIGO-D will require eccentric waveform models and template banks.
authors: Devesh Giri, Sajal Mukherjee, Apratim Ganguly, Sanjit Mitra

papers.title: Experimentally relevant witness for non-Markovianity in discrete time crystals
papers.abstract: Discrete time crystals (DTCs) are almost always analyzed under the Born-Markov approximation, in which the environment is memoryless. We show that a reservoir with a finite correlation time $\tau_m$ leaves an exact and strikingly simple imprint on the stroboscopic dynamics of DTCs, which can be used as an experimentally relevant witness for non-Markovianity. By analyzing a post-Markovian master equation we prove that the Floquet spectrum splits into the ordinary Markovian spectrum plus a replica of the purely unitary Floquet spectrum, uniformly contracted by $e^{-T/\tau_m}$, where $T$ is the drive period. Consequently, the DTC signal decay rate becomes independent of any system parameter once $\tau_m$ exceeds the Markovian lifetime of the DTC. The measured decay, and in particular its insensitivity to tunable system parameters, thus becomes a direct read-out of the reservoir correlation time. Below this threshold the dynamics is already non-Markovian, but the memory remains hidden in the decay. We confirm this in two structurally unrelated DTCs, a collective long-range model with incoherent pumping and a disorder-free Ising chain with dephasing, where a single estimator recovers $\tau_m$. The time crystal thereby witnesses the non-Markovianity of its own environment.
authors: Rahul Ghosh, Victor Mukherjee, Yonatan Dubi

papers.title: Non-factorisable Yangian Lax matrices through oscillators
papers.abstract: We construct oscillator realisations of Yangian Lax operators in type $A$, with particular interest in non-factorisable operators associated with prime snake modules. Our construction applies to finite-dimensional skew representations of $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$. We prove that these representations are generated by the tensor vacuum in suitably ordered tensor products of oscillator representations. Their Lax operators are obtained by restricting the corresponding products of linear oscillator Lax operators to these submodules. We determine the vacuum eigenvalues and Drinfeld polynomials, and give a determinant formula for the dimensions directly in terms of the highest loop weights. A $21$-dimensional example illustrates the construction, including an explicit basis and a transfer-matrix identity.

papers.title: Why Cassini's Oval Could Not Replace Kepler's Ellipse?
papers.abstract: In the later seventeenth century, Kepler's ellipse was not yet accepted. Ward claimed that Boulliau's conic hypothesis amounted to a Ptolemaic equant at the ellipse's empty focus, and built his own model on it. Around 1675--1680, Giovanni Domenico Cassini proposed another curve, the ``oval'', a genus-1 quartic with no closed-form Kepler equation; yet its eccentric anomaly shares exactly the leading coefficient of Kepler's, and its empty focus is, for the Sun, 38 times closer to a true equant than the ellipse's. Dynamically, Binet's formula shows that the force producing the oval under the area law departs from the inverse square by an index $\mathcal{D}(e)\sim3/(4e^2)$, depending on the oval's parameter $e$: no single exponent serves the whole family. This absence of universality, not of an area law, distinguishes it from the ellipse, and arguably explains why Cassini, the Acad\'emie and Leibniz kept the question open after the \emph{Principia} (1687).

papers.title: Quantum adiabatic and diabatic optimization: A Hilbert space engineering strategy with Rydberg arrays
papers.abstract: Neutral-atom arrays provide a versatile platform for encoding combinatorial optimization problems with arbitrary graph connectivity [Nguyen et al., PRX Quantum 4, 010316 (2023)]. Although the dynamics of individual encoding gadgets has been studied [Bombieri et al., PRX Quantum 6, 020306 (2025)], understanding annealing bottlenecks in larger networks remains challenging. We investigate how engineering the Hilbert-space geometry controls quantum annealing in a family of blockaded-chain models motivated by these encodings. While boundary terms encode the target maximum independent set problem, the bulk geometry induces an auxiliary optimization problem associated with independent sets of cliques. Spectrally, the energetics of the quantum system can be approximated by physically derived clique weights. When the target problem and the auxiliary problems are consistent, the low-energy modes lie predominantly within the target subspace. This spectral structure motivates a diabatic annealing strategy that exploits target-compatible excited states, as tested on the diamond-chain graph family. These results provide a framework for predicting annealing bottlenecks, and demonstrate Hilbert-space engineering as a strategy for improving neutral-atom quantum optimization protocols.

papers.title: On the blow-up of the one-particle Lieb-Thirring constant in dimension two
papers.abstract: We establish three-term asymptotics for the one-particle Lieb-Thirring constant in dimension two as $\gamma\to 0$ and identify, up to rescaling and symmetries, the profile of the asymptotically worst potential. The proof uses the well-known relation between the one-particle constant and an integral moment of optimizers of the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. Through the optimizers' characterization as positive, vanishing solutions of the nonlinear elliptic equation $-\Delta Q + Q = Q^{s}$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, the essence of the proof lies in the asymptotic analysis of solutions $Q$ as $s\to\infty$.

papers.title: Catalytic compression of classical communication in exact entanglement transformations
papers.abstract: Entanglement catalysis is usually associated with making otherwise impossible transformations possible. Here we show that it can also change how much classical communication a transformation requires. A catalyst, returned exactly and uncorrelated with the output, can reduce the message alphabet size required for exact transformations of bipartite pure states by a factor that grows without bound as the Schmidt rank increases. In the asymptotic many-copy regime, however, this advantage disappears at the level of the leading communication rate: the optimal catalytic and noncatalytic rates coincide. We characterize the optimal catalytic cost in terms of R\'enyi entropies, revealing how the entanglement structure of the source and target governs the finite-copy advantage. Our results establish reusable entanglement as a resource for compressing classical communication in quantum state manipulation.

papers.title: A Free Energy Approach to Modelling Disordered Hyperuniform Patterns
papers.abstract: We present a free-energy-based approach for modelling disordered hyperuniform patterns. Specifically, we devise a phase-field crystal model with a correlation kernel that simultaneously selects for a continuous range of degenerate wave modes. At small wave vectors, we construct the correlation function by inverting the Ornstein-Zernike relation to approximate the structure factor of a hyperuniform pattern. Our model demonstrates a crossover between liquid, crystalline, quasicrystalline, and long-lived disordered states depending on the specified free energy parameter and driving force. We show that, for a fixed driving force, the specific structures and wave vectors selected by the density field can be controlled by modulating the width of the correlation kernel. Furthermore, we show that the scaling of the low-wave-vector region of the correlation function can accurately reproduce a specified hyperuniform exponent, independently of the structural properties at larger wave numbers. Our results establish a free-energy-based framework for describing disordered hyperuniform states, demonstrating and enabling independent control over structural selection and long-wavelength density correlations.
authors: Alex Mamaev, Enno Igel, Axel Voigt, Marco Salvalaglio

papers.title: Sequential strategy for depolarizing strength estimation
papers.abstract: We study the advantages of applying a sequential strategy for enhancing the precision in estimating the strength $p$ of a depolarizing channel, using qudit and two-qubit probes. The sequential strategy requires that the same depolarizing channel is repeatedly applied $M$ times to the quantum probe. From the analysis of the probe's output state, both the quantum Fisher information (QFI) and its regularization RQFI, given from multiplication by $p$, are analyzed. We determine that in the limit of $p \to 0$, the QFI is {\it linearly amplified} with the number of channel repetitions. Instead, in the weak-noise regime, the QFI is maximized at a finite value of $M$. Then, the RQFI decreases more quickly with $p$ as $M$ increases. In particular, for two-qubit probes, the RQFI decreases with the depolarization strength proportionally to the amount of correlation between the qubits. The greater the number of channel repetitions, the wider the range of $p$ for which the initial state of the probe that allows for the maximization of the QFI is a separable state. We also show that a single qubit probe undergoing a sequential encoding protocol outperforms the optimal two-qubit single-round QFI for $M>3$ in the weak-noise regime.
authors: Yasir Mehmood, Enrico Trombetti, Marco Pezzutto, Stefano Gherardini

papers.title: Information Causality Defeats Every Finite NPA Level
papers.abstract: For every finite level of the Navascu\'es-Pironio-Ac\'in (NPA) hierarchy, we construct correlations that satisfy all its constraints but violate information causality. At each fixed level, one use of a binary-outcome correlation and one classical bit suffice for a violation that grows without bound as the number of measurement settings increases. Information causality bounds the information gained about independent database bits, summed over possible requests, by the length of the message. Quantum correlations obey the one-bit bound; the optimal information gain at any fixed NPA level grows logarithmically with the number of settings. The violation remains unbounded even when all outcome probabilities are positive and, for any fixed number of measurement settings on each side, every choice of those settings admits a local model. One communicated bit therefore exposes an unbounded gap between information causality and every finite NPA level.

papers.title: Heavy double-gluon quarkonium and $\overline{b}ggc$ mesons
papers.abstract: We investigate heavy double-gluon hybrid mesons, built from a heavy quark-antiquark pair and two valence gluons, using the two-point QCD sum rule method. The charmonium-like $\bar{c}GGc$ and bottomonium-like $\bar{b}GGb$ states are considered with $J^{PC}=0^{\pm\pm}$ and $1^{\pm\pm}$, whereas the open-flavor $\bar{b}GGc$ states are classified by $J^{P}=0^{\pm}$ and $1^{\pm}$. The currents with $J^{PC}=0^{+-}, 0^{--}, 1^{++}$, and $1^{-+}$ vanish identically, so sum rules are derived for the remaining four channels. The operator product expansion is carried out up to dimension twelve, and the Borel parameter and continuum threshold are fixed so that the pole contribution dominates and the OPE converges. The resulting masses lie in the ranges $M\simeq 6.2$--$6.7$~GeV for $\bar{c}GGc$, $M\simeq 12.0$--$12.2$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGb$, and $M\simeq 9.2$--$9.6$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGc$, and the current couplings are obtained for all channels. These predictions provide a basis for analyzing the strong decays of double-gluon hybrids and for interpreting future experimental data in the heavy-quark sector.
authors: G. Daylan Esmer, B. Barsbay, K. Azizi, H. Sundu, S. T\"{u}rkmen

papers.title: Carroll Double Copy
papers.abstract: We construct a double copy for Carroll gravity as the ``square'' of Carroll Yang-Mills theory at the linearised level. Starting from the convolutional double copy prescription in Lorentzian spacetime, we take the Carrollian limit $c \rightarrow 0$ to establish a double copy dictionary compatible both with symmetries and the corresponding equations of motion. Since this limit yields two distinct sectors, namely the electric and magnetic Carroll theories, we systematically investigate double copy constructions involving all possible combinations of these parent theories. To accommodate the time-independent on-shell configurations of the magnetic Carroll fields, we introduce a suitable regularisation procedure for the convolutional double copy. In addition, the covariance of the double copy under Carroll boosts requires an appropriate dressing of the fields, leading to the inclusion of a Goldstone-type object in the construction. We first develop the formalism using toy models involving scalar fields and then apply it to the double copy between linearised Carroll Yang-Mills theory and Carroll gravity.
authors: Sucheta Majumdar, Silvia Nagy, Giorgio Pizzolo

papers.title: Vanishing Relative Distance of Uniformly Random CSS LDPC Codes Built from Permutation Matrices
papers.abstract: Classical random regular low-density parity-check codes can have minimum distance growing linearly with block length. We study CSS check matrices formed as full $J\times L$ arrays of arbitrary $P\times P$ permutation matrices, sampled uniformly subject to commutation. For fixed column weight $J\ge3$ and fixed even row weight $L>2J$, we prove that the relative minimum distance converges to zero in probability as $P\to\infty$, with block length $n=LP$. We analyze the weight enumerators that count all nontrivial logical representatives after excluding stabilizers. A coefficientwise lower bound shows that, at every fixed relative weight $0<\alpha<1$ along even-weight sequences, exponentially many such representatives exist with high probability. Their typical and mean counts have exponent lower bound $h_2(\alpha)/2$, where $h_2$ is the binary entropy function. We compare this bound with the classical LDPC and dense CSS mean weight-distribution exponents. The existence, with high probability, of a logical operator below every fixed target weight $\delta n$ yields the distance conclusion.

papers.title: Quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures: Comparison between dispersively and directly coupled superconducting qubits
papers.abstract: The Rabi frequency of a two-level system is directly proportional to the electric field amplitude being incident on this system. Taking advantage of this relationship, it is possible to use two-level systems as quantitative sensors of electric fields. Here, we apply this concept to superconducting qubits and use them for quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures. Our superconducting circuit design includes three transmon qubits directly coupled to the central microwave feedline and three transmon qubits coupled dispersively via readout resonators to the feedline. We compare both coupling schemes to assess their reliability for microwave power sensing. Further, we describe the modeling behind each power-sensing method, including an uncertainty estimation based upon repeated measurements. By combining dispersively coupled and directly coupled qubits on the same device, we are able to explore different power ranges: from $-155\;$dBm to $-130\;$dBm for the directly coupled qubits and from $-95\;$dBm to $-55\;$dBm for the dispersively coupled qubits. When determining the microwave-line attenuation for a frequency of $6.0\;$GHz from room temperature to the millikelvin stage of the cryostat, we obtain best estimates and uncertainties for the directly coupled transmons of $(74.7\pm 0.2) \;$dB and for the dispersively coupled transmons of $(75.4\pm 6.8) \;$dB. The larger uncertainty of the dispersively coupled qubit measurements indicates that these qubits are less reliable for power sensing than the directly coupled qubits, most likely, due to the additional coupling resonator, whose transfer function is difficult to estimate accurately. Our results constitute the first step towards validation of qubit power sensing in dilution fridges, leading towards traceability for cryogenic microwave measurements.
authors: Asen L. Georgiev, Christoph Kissling, Fabian Kaap, Victor Gaydamachenko, Lukas Gr\"unhaupt, Mark Bieler

papers.title: Sharp $L_p$-Regularity for Quantum Markov Semigroups
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp universal constants in positive-input $L_p$-regularity for finite-dimensional quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful invariant state. For $1<p<\infty$, they are $p\sin(\pi/p)/(2(p-1))$ under KMS symmetry and $\frac{p}{2(p-1)}\tan(\frac{\pi}{2}\min\{1/p,1-1/p\})$ without a symmetry assumption, with the endpoint values at $p=1$ given by $\pi/2$ and $\pi/4$, respectively.

papers.title: Non-Canonical Q-balls in Polyattractor Inflation Models
papers.abstract: We show that Q-balls can exist in supergravity-based polyattractor inflation models that interpolate between $\alpha$-attractor T-models and polynomial attractor models. We consider both the original polyattractor potential and a natural generalisation. We find that Q-balls solutions exist when the model deviates significantly from the T-model $\alpha$-attractor, whereas in the T-model limit no Q-balls exist. These are non-canonical Q-balls due to the non-canonical kinetic term of the complex inflaton field. Such Q-balls could have significant cosmological consequences if they are produced at the end of inflation. In particular, if the global $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry of the supergravity-based polyattractor model is unbroken, the Q-balls can be absolutely stable and could account for dark matter.
authors: Kimberley Siret, Rhys Abercromby, Kit Lloyd-Stubbs, John McDonald

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning designs Quantum Repeater Protocols on Networks beyond the Chain Scenario
papers.abstract: Small-scale quantum repeater protocols have been shown to distribute entanglement over existing telecommunication infrastructure by means of short range quantum communications and long range classical messages. For larger networks, there are a number of theoretical proposals about how to operate the network to achieve a good performance under varying metrics. Moreover, since the dimension of the space of possible protocols grows exponentially with network size, plenty of those proposals are based on heuristics that reduce the search space. One of these is entanglement routing, which simplifies the problem on non-linear networks by allocating a series of disjoint paths and running chain protocols simultaneously on them. However, in this work we claim routing leads to suboptimal protocols. In fact, inspired by works on linear chains, we apply reinforcement learning to non-linear networks and optimize over the larger non-routing protocol space. Then, we find protocols that outperform a routed extension of the swap-ASAP protocol, even in the parameter regimes where the latter is widely recognized as the state of the art. These results indicate that routing must be discarded in favor of non-routing methods, while they pave the way towards the design of a sensible Quantum Internet architecture.
authors: Andr\'es Agust\'i Casado, \'Alvaro Troyano Olivas, Javier Faba Garc\'ia, Luis M. Robledo, Vicente Mart\'in, Laura Ortiz

papers.title: Rethinking Entropic Uncertainty: How measuring without a trace leads to longer keys
papers.abstract: In recent years, the entropic uncertainty relation (EUR) has been one of the most prominent tools to obtain tight key rates secure against general coherent attacks for a broad class of quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols. Despite its success, the fundamental question of how to incorporate the statistics of more than two mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) directly into the EUR is yet to be answered. Here, we introduce a simple yet powerful shift of perspective: Instead of the usual tripartition into the systems of Alice, Bob and Eve, we treat Alice and Bob as one joint system and introduce an additional register as the third system. This register contains the results of appropriately chosen virtual measurements that leave no trace in the real branch of the protocol, but act as a conditioning on the counterfactual phase error measurements. We show that this allows us to obtain tight key rates for QKD protocols using an arbitrary number of MUBs directly and natively from the EUR. Moreover, we demonstrate that this approach has a much broader relevance beyond the inclusion of multiple MUBs, allowing for improvements in many existing security proofs and the treatment of previously unexplored aspects for a wide range of protocols.

papers.title: Instant Folded Strings: Fractal Decay and ANEC Saturation
papers.abstract: Instant Folded Strings (IFSs) present a puzzle. On the one hand, they appear to be an intrinsic part of string theory: they are fundamental closed strings nucleated classically in backgrounds in which the string coupling grows toward the future, and they have been argued to play an important role in black-hole interiors and cosmology. On the other hand, their energy-momentum tensor violates the Averaged Null Energy Condition (ANEC), placing IFSs in tension with standard causality and unitarity arguments. We show that finite string coupling resolves this tension by triggering a decay cascade that saturates the ANEC in Minkowski spacetime. The remnant of the original IFS persists indefinitely, continuously seeding a self-similar fragmentation cascade that produces infinitely many strings over its full history. In the semiclassical regime, the cascade is governed by a single Malthusian exponent, $\kappa_{\mathrm{IFS}}=2\sqrt{2}-2$, which controls the branching growth, pressure decay, cutoff-ANEC convergence, and anomalous non-integer dependence on the string coupling. The complete state has vanishing total energy and momentum while remaining highly excited and carrying negative integrated pressure on every finite time slice. This provides a concrete example of genuinely stringy low-energy dynamics in which microscopic null-energy consistency coexists with macroscopic negative pressure.

papers.title: Geometry of squeezed states. The phase-space metric, relative vacua and cosmology
papers.abstract: Geometry enters quantum theory in two places. The space of quantum states carries a symplectic form, which generates unitary evolution, and a metric, which governs uncertainties and transition probabilities. The classical phase space acquires a metric of its own when a vacuum is chosen: quantizing a linear system amounts to choosing a compatible complex structure, equivalently a compatible metric $g$. We take this second metric as the primary object and show that it plays, on phase space, the role that the quantum metric plays on the space of states: fluctuations of linear observables are $g$-norms of Hamiltonian vector fields, and along coherent states $g/2\hbar$ \emph{is} the quantum metric. Squeezed states then have a simple description. A squeezed vacuum is the vacuum of another metric, and squeezing is a property of a pair of metrics, a relative vacuum, whose invariants are the eigenvalues $e^{\pm2r_i}$ of $L=g_0^{-1}g$. We work out the harmonic oscillator in detail, including why a rotated squeezed state no longer minimizes the product of the displayed uncertainties. Quadratic evolution deforms the metric, and only the part of the generator that is self-adjoint with respect to the reference changes the $r_i$, at a rate we give exactly. For fields, a vacuum is unitarily implementable relative to a reference exactly when it lies at finite distance from it in the space of vacua. For a massless field in de Sitter space we revisit the two canonical charts compared by Grain and Vennin: relative to the reference of the standard squeezing formalism the Bunch--Davies state has $\sinh r_k=1/(2|k\eta|)$, and relative to the vacuum that a radiation era beginning at time $\eta$ would select it has $\sinh r_k=1/(2k^2\eta^2)$. The second comparison squeezes twice as fast and is unitarily implementable; the first is not.

papers.title: Conditioned Reactive-Power Tuning Manifolds in Constrained Inverse Source Problems
papers.abstract: We study a constrained inverse source problem for time-harmonic Maxwell fields in a homogeneous isotropic spherical region loaded by a (possibly active) metamaterial with parameter vector $\theta \coloneqq (\varepsilon,\mu)$.
